brd_section.1.summary: Chapter 1 is the introduction; it holds the purpose, scope, audience, reading guide and definitions in its five sections.
brd_section.1.title: BRD 1 Introduction

brd_section.1.1.summary: Section 1.1 says the document specifies two connected systems for NRB Bank, the Loan Origination System and the Loan Management System, and that it is one document because the handoff between them is itself a control.
brd_section.1.1.title: BRD 1.1 Purpose

brd_section.1.2.summary: Section 1.2 is a heading only; what is in and out of scope is in its two sub-sections.
brd_section.1.2.title: BRD 1.2 Scope of this document

brd_section.1.2.1.summary: Section 1.2.1 lists what is in scope for the origination system, the servicing system and what both share.
brd_section.1.2.1.title: BRD 1.2.1 In scope

brd_section.1.2.2.summary: Section 1.2.2 says the platform is not the Core Banking System and lists six other things left out of the specification.
brd_section.1.2.2.title: BRD 1.2.2 Explicitly out of scope

brd_section.1.3.summary: Section 1.3 lists eight audiences for the BRD and the sections each should read first.
brd_section.1.3.title: BRD 1.3 Intended audience

brd_section.1.4.summary: Section 1.4 explains that the BRD states business needs, not technical design, and how requirement numbers, priorities and boxed notes work.
brd_section.1.4.title: BRD 1.4 How to read this document

brd_section.1.5.summary: Section 1.5 is the BRD's list of terms and abbreviations, from Advance payment to Write-off.
brd_section.1.5.title: BRD 1.5 Definitions and abbreviations

brd_section.10.summary: Section 10 lists the 37 business entities the two systems and the business share, in three tables: origination, servicing and shared.
brd_section.10.title: BRD 10 Key business data entities

brd_section.10.1.summary: Section 10.1 is a table of 16 origination entities, from Partner and Product to HandoffPackage, each with its purpose and notable attributes.
brd_section.10.1.title: BRD 10.1 Origination entities

brd_section.10.2.summary: Section 10.2 is a table of 16 servicing entities, from Loan and Demand to ReconciliationRun, each with its purpose and notable attributes.
brd_section.10.2.title: BRD 10.2 Servicing entities

brd_section.10.3.summary: Section 10.3 is a table of five entities shared by both systems: Configuration, AuditEvent, Exception, User and Role, and Notification.
brd_section.10.3.title: BRD 10.3 Shared entities

brd_section.11.summary: Section 11 proposes four delivery phases (origination, servicing core, risk and treatment, scale and extension), each with scope and a business outcome.
brd_section.11.title: BRD 11 Delivery phasing

brd_section.12.summary: Section 12 is a table of 25 things NRB must supply, each with the point at which it is needed.
brd_section.12.title: BRD 12 Dependencies on NRB Bank Limited

brd_section.13.summary: Section 13 is a table of 19 risks, each with a likelihood and impact rating and a mitigation.
brd_section.13.title: BRD 13 Risks and mitigations

brd_section.14.summary: Section 14 gives 48 business conditions for accepting each capability, written in Given/When/Then form, 30 for origination and 18 for servicing.
brd_section.14.title: BRD 14 Acceptance criteria

brd_section.14.1.summary: Section 14.1 gives 30 acceptance conditions for origination, from account validation and sampling to scoring, sanction and funding.
brd_section.14.1.title: BRD 14.1 Origination acceptance conditions

brd_section.14.2.summary: Section 14.2 gives 18 acceptance conditions for servicing, from the funded-loan handoff to case-file reproduction.
brd_section.14.2.title: BRD 14.2 Servicing acceptance conditions

brd_section.15.summary: Section 15 says that once the BRD is baselined, changes go through written change requests, assessed and signed, and deferred requirements go to a deferred-scope register.
brd_section.15.title: BRD 15 Change control

brd_section.2.summary: Chapter 2 gives the business context: the current state, the rationale, the objectives and the success measures.
brd_section.2.title: BRD 2 Business context and drivers

brd_section.2.1.summary: Section 2.1 names three constraints of the Bank's present lending operation: acquisition cost, document-bound origination and spreadsheet-based servicing.
brd_section.2.1.title: BRD 2.1 Current state

brd_section.2.2.summary: Section 2.2 says partner-sourced origination makes the product viable and the servicing system lets the Bank handle the volume, so the two are built together.
brd_section.2.2.title: BRD 2.2 Business rationale

brd_section.2.3.summary: Section 2.3 lists nine business objectives, OBJ-01 to OBJ-09, each with an owner.
brd_section.2.3.title: BRD 2.3 Business objectives

brd_section.2.4.summary: Section 2.4 sets nine success measures with targets, such as zero misdirected disbursements and batch validation in under ten minutes.
brd_section.2.4.title: BRD 2.4 Success measures

brd_section.3.summary: Chapter 3 gives the solution overview: how lending is split between the two systems, who owns what, the system landscape and the guiding principles.
brd_section.3.title: BRD 3 Solution overview

brd_section.3.1.summary: Section 3.1 splits the lending lifecycle at one point, the moment the Core Banking System confirms a disbursement: before it is origination, after it is servicing.
brd_section.3.1.title: BRD 3.1 Two systems, one lending lifecycle

brd_section.3.2.summary: Section 3.2 says the boundary is a business control: servicing accepts only a confirmed funded loan, and lists the six things the handoff carries.
brd_section.3.2.title: BRD 3.2 The ownership boundary

brd_section.3.3.summary: Section 3.3 describes six layers of the platform and states what it never does: hold a balance, post to the Bank's books or move money on its own authority.
brd_section.3.3.title: BRD 3.3 System landscape

brd_section.3.4.summary: Section 3.4 sets twelve guiding principles that bind the design, such as never holding money, unique keys on every instruction and configuration instead of code.
brd_section.3.4.title: BRD 3.4 Guiding business principles

brd_section.4.summary: Chapter 4 covers stakeholders, roles and governance: the stakeholder register, origination and servicing roles, and access control.
brd_section.4.title: BRD 4 Stakeholders, roles and governance

brd_section.4.1.summary: Section 4.1 is a register of eleven stakeholders with their interest in the programme and what each owns or does.
brd_section.4.1.title: BRD 4.1 Stakeholder register

brd_section.4.2.summary: Section 4.2 is a heading only; the origination and servicing roles are in its two sub-sections.
brd_section.4.2.title: BRD 4.2 Business roles

brd_section.4.2.1.summary: Section 4.2.1 lists nine origination roles, two at the partner and seven at NRB Bank, with the main duty of each.
brd_section.4.2.1.title: BRD 4.2.1 Origination roles

brd_section.4.2.2.summary: Section 4.2.2 lists nine servicing roles at NRB Bank, from Loan Manager to Auditor, with the main duty of each.
brd_section.4.2.2.title: BRD 4.2.2 Servicing roles

brd_section.4.3.summary: Section 4.3 holds nine access-control rules: roles, partner data separation, no self-approval, sampling-reviewer independence, a second login factor, protected personal data, idle-account shutdown, logging and approval limits.
brd_section.4.3.title: BRD 4.3 Access control and segregation of duties

brd_section.5.summary: Chapter 5 describes the end-to-end process: the narrative, the origination states, the servicing states and the handoff control.
brd_section.5.title: BRD 5 End-to-end business process

brd_section.5.1.summary: Section 5.1 tells the agricultural micro loan story in seventeen stages, from partner setup to closure, naming the system for each.
brd_section.5.1.title: BRD 5.1 Process narrative

brd_section.5.2.summary: Section 5.2 lists 23 origination statuses and five rules: only allowed changes, both amounts kept, only the origination system sanctions, idle applications expire, and every change is logged.
brd_section.5.2.title: BRD 5.2 Origination lifecycle states

brd_section.5.3.summary: Section 5.3 lists twelve states a loan can be in while it is serviced, and requires that every loan has exactly one current state with a full history.
brd_section.5.3.title: BRD 5.3 Servicing lifecycle states

brd_section.5.4.summary: Section 5.4 holds five rules for the handoff: one complete package, servicing accepts only a complete confirmed one, a repeat never creates a second loan, a daily comparison, and a controlled opening-balance load.
brd_section.5.4.title: BRD 5.4 The handoff control

brd_section.6.summary: Chapter 6 states what the origination system must do; it is a long chapter with eleven sections, and its depth is deliberately uneven.
brd_section.6.title: BRD 6 Business requirements — Loan Origination System

brd_section.6.1.summary: Section 6.1 holds seven rules for setting up a partner and each partner and product pair: its details, its limits, suspension, exposure ceiling, its users, risk-sharing terms and a performance view.
brd_section.6.1.title: BRD 6.1 Partner and product setup

brd_section.6.10.summary: Section 6.10 is a heading with two sub-sections, one for Bank oversight and one for partner visibility, holding ten requirements.
brd_section.6.10.title: BRD 6.10 Oversight and partner visibility

brd_section.6.10.1.summary: Section 6.10.1 holds four requirements for what Bank staff can see and do: full application detail, search, holds and an exceptions workspace.
brd_section.6.10.1.title: BRD 6.10.1 Bank oversight

brd_section.6.10.2.summary: Section 6.10.2 holds six requirements for what partners can see: their own applications, the detail they see and do not see, disbursed accounts, reports and a dashboard.
brd_section.6.10.2.title: BRD 6.10.2 Partner visibility

brd_section.6.11.summary: Section 6.11 holds six requirements for administration and configuration: users and roles, product settings, versioning, reference data and moving configuration between environments.
brd_section.6.11.title: BRD 6.11 Configuration and administration

brd_section.6.2.summary: Section 6.2 holds seven rules for bulk application files: a versioned template, whole-file rejection, limits shown first, row checks in three groups, browser corrections, partial submission and three-level duplicate detection.
brd_section.6.2.title: BRD 6.2 Bulk application submission

brd_section.6.2.1.summary: Section 6.2.1 is the table behind BR-LOS-116: three duplicate-detection scopes, what each matches on and how each is treated.
brd_section.6.2.1.title: BRD 6.2.1 Duplicate detection

brd_section.6.2.2.summary: Section 6.2.2 lists the 16 fields of a Phase 1 agricultural application and the business check for each; the BRD says the list will be revised.
brd_section.6.2.2.title: BRD 6.2.2 Application fields — Phase 1 agricultural product

brd_section.6.2.3.summary: Section 6.2.3 holds one rule: no application is accepted without a recorded borrower consent, and the BRD flags a legal question about what the consent must be.
brd_section.6.2.3.title: BRD 6.2.3 Borrower consent

brd_section.6.3.summary: Section 6.3 holds eight rules for checking the borrower's bank account before submission and again before payout, run as a queued background process.
brd_section.6.3.title: BRD 6.3 Pre-submission account validation

brd_section.6.3.1.summary: Section 6.3.1 lists nine validation outcomes with the message the partner sees and whether the problem can be put right.
brd_section.6.3.1.title: BRD 6.3.1 Validation outcomes presented to the partner

brd_section.6.4.summary: Section 6.4 holds fifteen rules for scoring every application against a scorecard that Credit Risk owns, and for how scores are recorded, used, overridden and reported.
brd_section.6.4.title: BRD 6.4 Application scoring

brd_section.6.4.1.summary: Section 6.4.1 shows four illustrative risk bands, each with its recommended decision and what happens next.
brd_section.6.4.1.title: BRD 6.4.1 Recommended decision bands

brd_section.6.5.summary: Section 6.5 holds eight rules for sampling: picking by a controlled random rate, a sound random source, a reproducible record, rate settings, system-decision records and mandatory rules.
brd_section.6.5.title: BRD 6.5 Sampling and credit oversight

brd_section.6.5.1.summary: Section 6.5.1 describes the review screen for a sampled application, with seven panels, and holds six rules for rejection reasons, records, deferral, the queue, reversal and quality figures.
brd_section.6.5.1.title: BRD 6.5.1 Reviewing a sampled application

brd_section.6.6.summary: Section 6.6 holds fourteen rules for sanction: how the proposed terms are set, automatic sanction inside thresholds, a credit approval queue, the approver's choices, authority limits, conditions, records and reports.
brd_section.6.6.title: BRD 6.6 Sanction and credit approval

brd_section.6.6.1.summary: Section 6.6.1 is the routing table for sanction: four cases, where each goes and how it is recorded.
brd_section.6.6.1.title: BRD 6.6.1 Sanction routing

brd_section.6.7.summary: Section 6.7 is the BRD's section on the field officer's work: it opens with the operating context and holds four sub-sections with 27 requirements.
brd_section.6.7.title: BRD 6.7 Field verification and evidence capture

brd_section.6.7.1.summary: Section 6.7.1 holds six requirements for the field officer's app: Android, one device per officer, two-factor login, two languages, one-handed use and no screenshots.
brd_section.6.7.1.title: BRD 6.7.1 Operating context and device

brd_section.6.7.2.summary: Section 6.7.2 holds five requirements for working offline, followed by a block that says four steps shall never proceed offline.
brd_section.6.7.2.title: BRD 6.7.2 Working without connectivity

brd_section.6.7.3.summary: Section 6.7.3 holds nine requirements for how an officer starts a verification and captures evidence, from KYC confirmation to the audit trail.
brd_section.6.7.3.title: BRD 6.7.3 Verification and evidence

brd_section.6.7.4.summary: Section 6.7.4 holds seven requirements on assigning sanctioned applications to field officers and managing the officers.
brd_section.6.7.4.title: BRD 6.7.4 Assignment and officer management

brd_section.6.8.summary: Section 6.8 holds eight requirements for the credit bureau check, which the BRD calls the step with the highest information-security sensitivity in origination.
brd_section.6.8.title: BRD 6.8 Credit bureau verification

brd_section.6.9.summary: Section 6.9 holds eleven requirements for approval, loan account opening and disbursement, the point where the BRD says the platform causes money to move.
brd_section.6.9.title: BRD 6.9 Approval, loan account opening and disbursement

brd_section.7.summary: Section 7 is the BRD's overview of the Loan Management System: what it runs after payout and the one constraint that governs all of it.
brd_section.7.title: BRD 7 Business requirements — Loan Management System

brd_section.7.1.summary: Section 7.1 says the LMS starts only from a loan that is confirmed paid out, and that it keeps one complete record for each such loan.
brd_section.7.1.title: BRD 7.1 Funded-loan handoff and booking

brd_section.7.10.summary: Section 7.10 covers late payment from first day to loss: counting days past due, grading loans, setting money aside, suspending income, write-off, freezing and collections.
brd_section.7.10.title: BRD 7.10 Delinquency, classification and provisioning

brd_section.7.11.summary: Section 7.11 says a settlement, waiver or write-off needs a shown figure, approval within delegated authority and a complete record, and that a write-off never destroys history.
brd_section.7.11.title: BRD 7.11 Settlement, write-off and recovery

brd_section.7.12.summary: Section 7.12 covers the partner side of co-lending: who the partners are, their shares, their schedules, their credit notes and their reports.
brd_section.7.12.title: BRD 7.12 Co-lending and partner economics

brd_section.7.13.summary: Section 7.13 covers running the whole loan book: moving loans between branches, credit-line limits, batch states, exception queues and job alerts.
brd_section.7.13.title: BRD 7.13 Portfolio operations

brd_section.7.14.summary: Section 7.14 says a loan closes only after its balances are cleared, the CBS agrees, collateral is released and an authorised user has approved.
brd_section.7.14.title: BRD 7.14 Closure

brd_section.7.2.summary: Section 7.2 says loan behaviour must come from product configuration that business users can change under maker-checker, without a software release.
brd_section.7.2.title: BRD 7.2 Product and servicing configuration

brd_section.7.3.summary: Section 7.3 says schedules are versioned and never overwritten, so the bank can explain later why a borrower owed what they owed.
brd_section.7.3.title: BRD 7.3 Repayment schedule management

brd_section.7.4.summary: Section 7.4 says the LMS raises the bills (demands) on their due dates, never deletes or quietly changes one, and sends the accounting effect to the CBS.
brd_section.7.4.title: BRD 7.4 Demand, billing and charges

brd_section.7.5.summary: Section 7.5 says interest is counted every period, penalty interest is kept apart, and unpaid interest on bad loans stops counting as income.
brd_section.7.5.title: BRD 7.5 Interest and accrual management

brd_section.7.6.summary: Section 7.6 makes repricing a floating-rate portfolio safe: a practice run, two people, a new schedule version for each loan and no rewriting of paid history.
brd_section.7.6.title: BRD 7.6 Interest-rate repricing

brd_section.7.7.summary: Section 7.7 says what must hold for every payment once the bank knows it has arrived, and leaves the question of how a payment reaches the system to NRB.
brd_section.7.7.title: BRD 7.7 Repayment, collection and allocation

brd_section.7.7.1.summary: Section 7.7.1 lists what must be true for every known payment, whatever channel it came through.
brd_section.7.7.1.title: BRD 7.7.1 Requirements that hold whatever the channel

brd_section.7.7.2.summary: Section 7.7.2 lists seven questions the bank must answer before repayment collection can be designed, and none of them is a requirement yet.
brd_section.7.7.2.title: BRD 7.7.2 Open items for NRB Bank Limited

brd_section.7.8.summary: Section 7.8 says collateral must be recorded, valued, watched for shortfall and released only after checks and approval.
brd_section.7.8.title: BRD 7.8 Collateral and security servicing

brd_section.7.9.summary: Section 7.9 covers changes to a running loan: paying early, restructuring, manual adjustments and refunds, each with limits, approvals and a record.
brd_section.7.9.title: BRD 7.9 Prepayment, restructuring and adjustments

brd_section.8.summary: Section 8 sets out what reporting the platform must provide: origination and servicing reports, Bangladesh Bank returns and reconciliation.
brd_section.8.title: BRD 8 Reporting, MIS and regulatory obligations

brd_section.8.1.summary: Section 8.1 asks for an origination dashboard, a standard set of origination reports, and a way to export, schedule and email reports.
brd_section.8.1.title: BRD 8.1 Origination reporting

brd_section.8.2.summary: Section 8.2 lists 14 servicing reports with their purpose, then asks for a servicing dashboard, report headers that state how the report was produced, and export and scheduling.
brd_section.8.2.title: BRD 8.2 Servicing reporting and statements

brd_section.8.3.summary: Section 8.3 asks for the extracts and returns the bank files with Bangladesh Bank, their retention, and dated versioning of regulatory rules.
brd_section.8.3.title: BRD 8.3 Bangladesh Bank regulatory obligations

brd_section.8.4.summary: Section 8.4 asks for a daily comparison with the core banking system, ownership and documented closure of every difference, an internal consistency check and an audit trail.
brd_section.8.4.title: BRD 8.4 Reconciliation

brd_section.9.summary: Section 9 sets out how the platform reaches the outside systems it depends on, from the core banking system to the SMS gateway.
brd_section.9.title: BRD 9 Integration requirements

brd_section.9.1.summary: Section 9.1 is a table of five outside parties the platform depends on, how each is reached, what it is for and how critical it is.
brd_section.9.1.title: BRD 9.1 Integration inventory

brd_section.9.2.summary: Section 9.2 states that the core banking system has no programmatic interface, that robotic process automation is the only route, and six business consequences the bank is asked to accept knowingly.
brd_section.9.2.title: BRD 9.2 Core Banking System: the constraint and the approach

brd_section.9.2.1.summary: Section 9.2.1 lists 12 operations the platform performs on the core banking system, from account enquiry and loan account opening to a single adapter.
brd_section.9.2.1.title: BRD 9.2.1 Core Banking System operations

brd_section.9.3.summary: Section 9.3 sets 13 controls on the robotic process automation that drives the core banking system: where it runs, who it signs in as, how it is watched and what happens when it fails.
brd_section.9.3.title: BRD 9.3 Robotic process automation controls

brd_section.9.4.summary: Section 9.4 sets three rules for the handoff of a funded loan from origination to servicing and for the status that flows back.
brd_section.9.4.title: BRD 9.4 Origination to servicing

brd_section.9.5.summary: Section 9.5 sets four rules for the bureau inquiry: where it runs, how it is monitored, how its credentials are kept apart and how it is logged.
brd_section.9.5.title: BRD 9.5 Credit Information Bureau

brd_section.9.6.summary: Section 9.6 sets five rules for checking applicant identity: the election database check, liveness, face comparison, protection of images and behaviour when verification is down.
brd_section.9.6.title: BRD 9.6 Electronic KYC and identity

brd_section.9.7.summary: Section 9.7 sets five rules for notifications: SMS passcodes, borrower notices in Bangla and English, failure handling, what a passcode message may hold, and the bank's confirmation of channels and templates.
brd_section.9.7.title: BRD 9.7 Notifications

bridge.BR-LMS-100.summary: Partly covered. A loan and its payout record can be created. In the test, nothing checked that the handover was complete and nothing refused an incomplete one.

bridge.BR-LMS-101.summary: Covered. The Loan form links the schedule, bills, payments, security, adjustments, logs and accounting records. Accounting entries are reached through the ledger rather than the form.
bridge.BR-LMS-101.title: One record holds everything about a loan

bridge.BR-LMS-102.summary: Covered. The loan has a Status field with a value for each BRD stage, under different names. In the test, it kept no history of status changes.
bridge.BR-LMS-102.title: The stages of a loan's life

bridge.BR-LMS-103.summary: Covered. The product supplies the rules, but the interest rate and the penalty rate on a loan can still be typed over (in the test, with no warning).
bridge.BR-LMS-103.title: Rules come from the product, not from each loan

bridge.BR-LMS-104.summary: Covered. The loan keeps the sanctioned Loan Amount apart from the Disbursed Amount, and credit lines also show maximum, used and available limit.
bridge.BR-LMS-104.title: Track the approved limit separately from what was taken

bridge.BR-LMS-105.summary: Partly covered. A loan can be imported with opening balances, but there is no control-total check or sign-off, and the standard import mapping is wrong (DEF-6).
bridge.BR-LMS-105.title: Bring existing loans over from the old system, and prove the totals match

bridge.BR-LMS-106.summary: Covered. The product holds a Loan Category and each loan fetches it.
bridge.BR-LMS-106.title: Each loan has a category for reports

bridge.BR-LMS-110.summary: Covered. The Repayment Schedule Type offers a choice for each of the five methods. One defect was found in the flat-interest schedule.
bridge.BR-LMS-110.title: Five ways of working out repayments

bridge.BR-LMS-111.summary: Partly covered. The rate and the day-count method are stored, but there is no fixed or floating flag, no reference rate and no repricing frequency.
bridge.BR-LMS-111.title: Store the interest rate, how it is calculated, and whether it is fixed or floating

bridge.BR-LMS-112.summary: Partly covered. The moratorium works on each loan, but the Loan Product has no moratorium field, so the rule is typed on the loan. The coverage analysis rated it covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-112.title: Payment holiday (moratorium) rules

bridge.BR-LMS-113.summary: Partly covered. The product can name a fee and its accounts, but its percentage, amount and basis are not read by the code, so the rule raises no fee. The coverage analysis rated it covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-113.title: Rules for fees and charges

bridge.BR-LMS-114.summary: Partly covered. The four payment orders can be set. In the test, the Interest component was never paid, one order paid a bill twice, and the Company logic setting is not read. The coverage analysis rated it covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-114.title: The order in which a payment is used

bridge.BR-LMS-115.summary: Partly covered. A Company switch turns loan accounting on or off and a consolidation option reduces posting volume, but 16.5.1 has no code that posts to the CBS.
bridge.BR-LMS-115.title: Two ways of keeping the accounts

bridge.BR-LMS-116.summary: Covered. The Loan Product has a Loan Partners field, and each Loan Partner holds its share and base rate. The Loan Partner record carries a beta flag.
bridge.BR-LMS-116.title: Link co-lending partners to the product

bridge.BR-LMS-117.summary: Gap. A product edit is saved at once, with no effective date, no approval step and no version number on the loans.
bridge.BR-LMS-117.title: Product rules have versions, start dates and approval

bridge.BR-LMS-120.summary: Covered. The repayment plan is built and submitted with the loan disbursement. In NRB's flow, booking and disbursement happen together, which D1 handles.
bridge.BR-LMS-120.title: Build the first repayment plan

bridge.BR-LMS-121.summary: Covered. Each schedule row stores principal, interest, total payment and the balance left.
bridge.BR-LMS-121.title: Each row shows the split

bridge.BR-LMS-122.summary: Covered. Each confirmed tranche creates a new schedule, and the earlier one is set to Outdated.
bridge.BR-LMS-122.title: Rebuild the plan when money is paid out in parts

bridge.BR-LMS-123.summary: Covered. A co-lent loan's schedule carries the partner rate and share and a Co-Lender Schedule table with one row per instalment.
bridge.BR-LMS-123.title: Keep a partner's plan for co-lent loans

bridge.BR-LMS-124.summary: Partly covered. A draft Loan Restructure shows a new plan before it is submitted, but each trial leaves draft records behind.
bridge.BR-LMS-124.title: "What-if" view with nothing saved

bridge.BR-LMS-125.summary: Partly covered. The old plan is kept with a new status, but it has no link to the plan that replaced it.
bridge.BR-LMS-125.title: Never overwrite an old plan

bridge.BR-LMS-126.summary: Gap. In the test, a schedule was submitted with no restructure at all, and the loan ended with two Active plans. The coverage analysis rated it partly covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-126.title: Only an approved change may rebuild a plan

bridge.BR-LMS-130.summary: Covered. A daily Process Loan Demand run raises demands of six types on their due dates.
bridge.BR-LMS-130.title: Raise the bills on their due dates

bridge.BR-LMS-131.summary: Partly covered. Fees can be attached by hand, but in the test a fee set to be added to the first repayment was not billed. The coverage analysis rated it covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-131.title: Attach fees to the loan

bridge.BR-LMS-132.summary: Partly covered. A due-details API and a Loan Outstanding Report give amounts as at a date, but the report has no penalty or charge columns.
bridge.BR-LMS-132.title: "What is owed on this date" view

bridge.BR-LMS-133.summary: Partly covered. A submitted bill is cancelled, not deleted, and stays visible, but in the test a cancel needed no reason and no approver.
bridge.BR-LMS-133.title: Never delete or quietly change a bill

bridge.BR-LMS-134.summary: Gap (needs the CBS link). 16.5.1 has no code that sends bills to the CBS, and no field holds a CBS journal number.
bridge.BR-LMS-134.title: Send bills to the CBS and keep its journal number

bridge.BR-LMS-135.summary: Partly covered. A failure on one loan is logged and rolled back, and a re-run does not duplicate bills, but there is no per-loan result list and no resume action.
bridge.BR-LMS-135.title: Bill-raising runs as a batch that can restart

bridge.BR-LMS-140.summary: Covered. A daily Process Loan Interest Accrual run counts interest from the balance, rate and the Company day-count convention.
bridge.BR-LMS-140.title: Count interest every day (accrual)

bridge.BR-LMS-141.summary: Partly covered. Penal interest is tracked in its own rows and accounts, but the amount billed is not the product's penal rate, and a payment inside the grace days can still pay penalty. The coverage analysis rated it covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-141.title: Penalty interest, kept separate

bridge.BR-LMS-142.summary: Covered. The product chooses how the interest for the odd days is recovered, and the test showed it added to the first instalment.
bridge.BR-LMS-142.title: Interest for odd days (broken period)

bridge.BR-LMS-143.summary: Partly covered. Loan Accrual Repost restores missing ledger entries but does not reverse and redo interest, and it has no approval step. The coverage analysis rated it covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-143.title: Undo and redo interest for a period, with approval

bridge.BR-LMS-144.summary: Covered. When a loan becomes NPA, the unpaid interest and charges move to suspense. Catch-up runs move too little.
bridge.BR-LMS-144.title: Stop counting interest as income on bad loans

bridge.BR-LMS-145.summary: Gap. In the test, none of the lending reports reconciles interest between the plan, bills, accruals, income and the ledger.
bridge.BR-LMS-145.title: Check that interest numbers agree everywhere

bridge.BR-LMS-150.summary: Gap. There is no selection screen for repricing, and the bulk rate code found is a leftover class with no document type.
bridge.BR-LMS-150.title: Choose which loans to reprice

bridge.BR-LMS-151.summary: Gap. For one loan the restructure date acts as the effective date, but there is no effective date for a bulk rate change.
bridge.BR-LMS-151.title: The new rate starts on a set date

bridge.BR-LMS-152.summary: Partly covered. For one loan the paid history is kept, but the unpaid part is rebuilt wrongly and the loan's paid totals are reset.
bridge.BR-LMS-152.title: Never change what is already paid

bridge.BR-LMS-153.summary: Partly covered. Both options exist on a single Loan Restructure, but only for one loan at a time, and the default term is the original term.
bridge.BR-LMS-153.title: Two repricing options

bridge.BR-LMS-154.summary: Gap. There is no batch dry run; a single loan can only be previewed through a draft Loan Restructure.
bridge.BR-LMS-154.title: A practice run first

bridge.BR-LMS-155.summary: Gap. There is no repricing run to approve, and one user can submit and approve a restructure.
bridge.BR-LMS-155.title: One person prepares, another approves

bridge.BR-LMS-156.summary: Partly covered. For one loan the old plan is kept and the new one is linked to its restructure, but not for a bulk run, and the old plan has no link forward.
bridge.BR-LMS-156.title: Each repriced loan gets a new plan version

bridge.BR-LMS-157.summary: Gap. There is no repricing batch, and in the test a second stale restructure for the same change was applied on top of the first.
bridge.BR-LMS-157.title: The repricing batch is safe to run and rerun

bridge.BR-LMS-158.summary: Gap. There is no batch to skip loans from, and a single restructure checks neither the rate type, nor the freeze, nor the loan status.
bridge.BR-LMS-158.title: Skip loans that shouldn't be repriced, automatically

bridge.BR-LMS-159.summary: Gap. There is no repricing event to send a notice from, although a Frappe Notification could be set up on an approved restructure.
bridge.BR-LMS-159.title: Tell the borrowers

bridge.BR-LMS-160.summary: Covered. The Loan Repayment form has a field for every item the BRD lists. The one limit is that Posting Date is always set by the system.
bridge.BR-LMS-160.title: Record a confirmed payment with full details

bridge.BR-LMS-161.summary: Partly covered. A draft repayment changes nothing, which is a usable workaround, but there is no pending status and no CBS confirmation step.
bridge.BR-LMS-161.title: A payment counts only after the CBS confirms it

bridge.BR-LMS-162.summary: Gap. Reference Number exists but is not unique, and the test showed one reference accepted twice, with both payments posted to the accounts.
bridge.BR-LMS-162.title: Apply each payment only once

bridge.BR-LMS-163.summary: Covered. A back-dated repayment cancels penalty after the value date and rewrites the days-past-due history from that date.
bridge.BR-LMS-163.title: Use the date the money actually arrived

bridge.BR-LMS-164.summary: Partly covered. The split is shown line by line, but a payment order (offset order) that uses the Interest component never pays interest. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-164.title: Split the payment in the set order and show it

bridge.BR-LMS-165.summary: Covered. The Repayment Type list has 20 options, including every type the BRD names. Pre Payment and Advance Payment also reshape the schedule.
bridge.BR-LMS-165.title: All the payment types the bank needs

bridge.BR-LMS-166.summary: Partly covered. There is a bulk posting method and a log per loan, but no upload screen, no validate-all-first step and no resume.
bridge.BR-LMS-166.title: Upload many payments in one file

bridge.BR-LMS-167.summary: Partly covered. ERPNext keeps unreconciled bank transactions that can be matched to repayments, but there is no owner, ageing or reason, and no create-repayment action in 16.5.1.
bridge.BR-LMS-167.title: Money nobody can match goes to a queue

bridge.BR-LMS-168.summary: Partly covered. The Loan Repayment form quotes a payoff by repayment type and date, but the figure shown and what a closure books can differ. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-168.title: How much to close today?

bridge.BR-LMS-169.summary: Covered. Loan Repayment Repost redoes postings and keeps the originals. It has no approval step or reason field, which is configuration the bank must add.
bridge.BR-LMS-169.title: Fix wrong payment postings safely

bridge.BR-LMS-170c.summary: Partly covered. Frappe Lending keeps security types, securities and dated prices with a haircut, but a nested price row is accepted and the per-security value fields stay empty. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-170c.title: A master list of collateral

bridge.BR-LMS-170r.summary: Gap (needs the CBS link). Frappe Lending has no feed of CBS transactions, so it cannot see a payment or reversal made directly in the CBS.
bridge.BR-LMS-170r.title: Catch payments made directly in the CBS

bridge.BR-LMS-171c.summary: Partly covered. The pledge statuses match the BRD, but in the test only Pledge Requested and Pledged were used, there is no approval step, and a secured loan was disbursed with no pledge. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-171c.title: The life of a pledge

bridge.BR-LMS-171r.summary: Gap (needs the CBS link). There is no end-to-end payment match report, and the unique CBS reference it would rely on is not enforced.
bridge.BR-LMS-171r.title: Match every payment end to end

bridge.BR-LMS-172.summary: Partly covered. Frappe Lending finds a real shortfall exactly, but the run cannot be limited to one loan, makes two records per exposure and, in the test, flagged borrowers who had no collateral. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-172.title: Watch for a collateral shortfall

bridge.BR-LMS-173.summary: Partly covered. A shortfall record is closed by the app when security is added or a payment is made, but it has no remedy type, owner, due date or approved exception, and it can close too early or too much.
bridge.BR-LMS-173.title: Track how a shortfall is fixed

bridge.BR-LMS-174.summary: Partly covered. A release request is checked against the loan, but approval re-checks nothing, two requests can be stacked past the limit, and a whitelisted call releases an assignment with no check. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-174.title: Release collateral only after checks and approval

bridge.BR-LMS-175.summary: Covered. Four standard reports show the status, the exposure, the exposure by borrower and the ledger of collateral. They have gaps in the detail but each ran on live data.
bridge.BR-LMS-175.title: Collateral reports

bridge.BR-LMS-180.summary: Partly covered. Frappe Lending has an Advance Payment type and a product setting, but it books the money as the next instalment paid early and does not cover the EMIs after it. The product's Reduce EMI choice is recorded and not applied. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-180.title: Paying future EMIs early (advance payment)

bridge.BR-LMS-181.summary: Partly covered. A Pre Payment type and a prepayment charge table exist, but the loan always keeps its EMI and ends sooner. There is no choice of a lower EMI, and the charge is typed in by hand.
bridge.BR-LMS-181.title: Paying extra to cut the loan (prepayment)

bridge.BR-LMS-182.summary: Partly covered. A Loan Restructure changes rate, term, EMI and the treatment of overdue amounts, with a type recorded. The types are not the regulator's, and a restructure re-ages the loan to zero days past due.
bridge.BR-LMS-182.title: Changing the terms for a struggling borrower (restructuring)

bridge.BR-LMS-183.summary: Covered. Approving a restructure marks the old Loan Repayment Schedule as Restructured or Rescheduled and activates a new one. The new plan's figures have flaws that the ledger does not share.
bridge.BR-LMS-183.title: A restructure makes a new plan and keeps the old one

bridge.BR-LMS-184.summary: Gap. The pieces of a limit exist (a Company percentage, a log, a monthly job), but in the test the job could not select any loan and wrote no log row, and nothing checks a limit when a restructure is approved. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-184.title: Limits on how much can be restructured

bridge.BR-LMS-185.summary: Partly covered. Waivers, capitalisations, a carry-forward type and a Loan Balance Adjustment exist, but one user can make and submit each, no approver or before and after amounts are stored, and a balance adjustment accepts any account and any amount.
bridge.BR-LMS-185.title: Manual corrections need two people and a full record

bridge.BR-LMS-186.summary: Partly covered. A Loan Refund pays back an excess amount and keeps a reference number, and an over-refund is refused, but there is no approval step. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-186.title: Refund overpayments, with approval

bridge.BR-LMS-187.summary: Covered. A Loan Security Deposit is created at disbursement, used by a repayment type and paid back through a Loan Refund. A Loan Closure repayment does not touch it, and the deposit is a per-disbursement tick, not a product setting.
bridge.BR-LMS-187.title: Track a security deposit

bridge.BR-LMS-188.summary: Gap. Frappe Lending has no Bangladesh Bank report of restructures, reschedules or waivers and no field for the regulatory treatment. The only related feature is the watch period after a restructure of an NPA loan.
bridge.BR-LMS-188.title: Report restructures and waivers to Bangladesh Bank

bridge.BR-LMS-190.summary: Covered. A daily classification run works out days past due for each loan and writes one Days Past Due Log row per loan per day. The history can be rewritten by back-dated payments and edited by two roles without a trace.
bridge.BR-LMS-190.title: Count days late every day, and keep the history

bridge.BR-LMS-191.summary: Partly covered. The bands are a table on the Company and the run grades each loan from them, but the only override is the Manual NPA tick, with no reason or approver, and the grade itself cannot be changed.
bridge.BR-LMS-191.title: Give each loan a health grade

bridge.BR-LMS-192.summary: Partly covered. Moves into and out of NPA are logged, but a change of grade such as STD to SMA leaves no record, and the logs can be edited or deleted without a trace.
bridge.BR-LMS-192.title: Keep the history of grade changes

bridge.BR-LMS-193.summary: Gap. The Company holds a table of provision rates by grade and security type, but nothing in the app reads a rate, calculates a provision or stores a basis.
bridge.BR-LMS-193.title: Set money aside for expected losses (provisioning)

bridge.BR-LMS-194.summary: Partly covered. Interest is moved to suspense automatically when a loan turns NPA, but collections while it stays NPA release nothing, and the whole amount is released at once only when the loan is upgraded, settled or written off. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-194.title: Unpaid interest waits in suspense

bridge.BR-LMS-195.summary: Covered. The Company has a separate setting, Days Past Due Threshold for Auto Write Off, and the nightly classification writes a loan off when it passes it. The setting is one value for the whole company, and a manual write-off is checked only against the pending principal, not against a threshold.
bridge.BR-LMS-195.title: Write-off has its own trigger

bridge.BR-LMS-196.summary: Partly covered. A freeze tick and a Loan Freeze Log stop accruals and bills, but the log has no approver, no reason and no record of what stopped, and unfreezing back-charges the frozen period.
bridge.BR-LMS-196.title: Freezing a loan

bridge.BR-LMS-197.summary: Gap. The bands and rates are rows on the Company form. They have no version, effective date or approval, and no grade or provision stores which rules it used.
bridge.BR-LMS-197.title: Grade, provision and income rules are owned and versioned

bridge.BR-LMS-198.summary: Gap. Frappe Lending 16.5.1 has no collections documents at all; the Collection Case, Collection Activity, Promise to Pay and Dunning Rule documents exist only in the develop branch (develop only). The original analysis said partly covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-198.title: Chasing late payers (collections)

bridge.BR-LMS-200.summary: Partly covered. The Loan Repayment form shows the make-up of a settlement before it is submitted, but there is no settlement proposal and nothing is held for approval. A Full Settlement creates the waivers and write-off for what is left unpaid when it is submitted; any repayment short by no more than the product's Auto Write Off Amount, a Partial Settlement included, also gets an automatic waiver on submit.
bridge.BR-LMS-200.title: Work out a settlement offer and show its make-up

bridge.BR-LMS-201.summary: Partly covered. Frappe's workflow feature could give approval by amount and role, but no workflow is set up, and no limit exists except two small product settings. The automatic write-off is submitted by the system with no approver.
bridge.BR-LMS-201.title: Approval limits for settlements, waivers and write-offs

bridge.BR-LMS-202.summary: Covered. A Loan Write Off changes the loan's status and posts the loss, and the loan, its schedule, demands, accruals and logs all stay. After a write-off the loan keeps accruing and loses its grade.
bridge.BR-LMS-202.title: A write-off keeps the history

bridge.BR-LMS-203.summary: Covered. Write Off Recovery and Write Off Settlement are the only repayment types accepted on a written-off loan, apart from waivers the system creates, and the money is credited to a recovery account on the original loan. A recovery is not capped, and an amount beyond the open principal is booked as a new interest demand.
bridge.BR-LMS-203.title: Money collected after a write-off

bridge.BR-LMS-204.summary: Gap (needs the CBS link). Frappe Lending posts these entries in its own ledger. It has no link to send them to a CBS and no field to keep a CBS journal reference.
bridge.BR-LMS-204.title: Send settlements and write-offs to the CBS

bridge.BR-LMS-205.summary: Partly covered. A Loan Repayment keeps a reference number, free-text remarks and the amounts payable and paid, but there is no approver, approval date, reason or before and after record. The Loan Write Off has no reference, reason or remarks field at all.
bridge.BR-LMS-205.title: Full record for every settlement, waiver, write-off and recovery

bridge.BR-LMS-210.summary: Covered. The Loan Partner master holds the partner's name, code, addresses, share, rate and FLDG terms, and checks the percentages. The FLDG fields are data only: nothing in the app acts on them.
bridge.BR-LMS-210.title: A list of co-lending partners

bridge.BR-LMS-211.summary: Covered. A Loan Product lists its partners in a Co Lending tab, the partner is chosen on the Loan, and the share works. The share is one figure on the partner, not one per product.
bridge.BR-LMS-211.title: Which products each partner joins, and its share

bridge.BR-LMS-212.summary: Partly covered. A Co-Lender Schedule is built beside the borrower's plan and each EMI is split, but a Loan Closure on a co-lent loan posts nothing to the partner. The document named Loan Partner Adhoc Charges Shared is not used by any code. The original analysis said covered.
bridge.BR-LMS-212.title: The partner's share of each plan and of charges

bridge.BR-LMS-213.summary: Partly covered. The app can show what is payable to each partner from the ledger through one interface call, but it has no partner settlement document, no scheduled reconciliation and no report of unmatched items. The hourly credit-note job has nothing to do with partners.
bridge.BR-LMS-213.title: Partner settlements and checks

bridge.BR-LMS-214.summary: Gap. Frappe Lending has no co-lending report. One interface call returns payable amounts per loan from the ledger, but it is not a report and shows the whole loan's figures, not the partner's.
bridge.BR-LMS-214.title: Partner reports

bridge.BR-LMS-220.summary: Covered. This verdict comes from reading the code and was not tested live. A Loan Transfer sets a new branch on many loans and keeps the same record, but it works only after Branch is set up as an accounting dimension.
bridge.BR-LMS-220.title: Move loans between branches in bulk

bridge.BR-LMS-221.summary: Partly covered. The three limit figures work and the movements made by booking, limit changes, disbursements and repayments are logged, but cancellations are not, the log has no reason or approver, does not log date changes, and its rows can be edited or deleted.
bridge.BR-LMS-221.title: Credit-line limits and their change log

bridge.BR-LMS-222.summary: Covered. A daily job closes every active credit-line loan whose end date has passed and whose utilised limit is 0. It has no setting on the product.
bridge.BR-LMS-222.title: Close repaid credit lines automatically

bridge.BR-LMS-223.summary: Partly covered. Only the Loan Repayment Repost has the five states, and only the bulk payment call keeps a result per loan. The runs for interest, bills, grades, accounting and shortfall have no status and no result per loan. A re-run after a failure was safe in the test.
bridge.BR-LMS-223.title: Every batch has a clear status

bridge.BR-LMS-224.summary: Gap. Failures go to Frappe's Error Log. An owner can be assigned by hand and an age can be read, but there is no queue for each kind of failure, no closure note and no count.
bridge.BR-LMS-224.title: Work queues for things that went wrong

bridge.BR-LMS-225.summary: Partly covered. Frappe records job runs and errors, and ships an Error Log notification that is switched off. No code in the lending app alerts anyone when a job fails.
bridge.BR-LMS-225.title: Alerts when jobs fail

bridge.BR-LMS-230.summary: Partly covered. A Loan Closure checks the amount paid, but it accepts a shortfall up to the product's Auto Write Off Amount and a future closure date, and the Request Loan Closure button works out a lower figure.
bridge.BR-LMS-230.title: Check everything is cleared before closing

bridge.BR-LMS-231.summary: Gap (needs the CBS link). Nothing in the closure path calls an outside banking service, and the app has no field to hold a CBS balance.
bridge.BR-LMS-231.title: Check the core bank before confirming closure

bridge.BR-LMS-232.summary: Partly covered. A Loan Security Release works and shows in the Loan Security Ledger report, but approving it overwrites the loan's closure date with today's date. Any Loan Manager can set the approval.
bridge.BR-LMS-232.title: Release collateral at closure

bridge.BR-LMS-233.summary: Covered. A Loan Refund returns an excess payment or a security deposit, posts the entries and keeps a reference number. The reference number is not mandatory, and a full excess refund closes the loan.
bridge.BR-LMS-233.title: Refund what is left

bridge.BR-LMS-234.summary: Partly covered. A Loan Closure Requested status exists, but nothing approves the step. Several routes close a loan with no request at all, and no approver is recorded.
bridge.BR-LMS-234.title: Closure needs approval

bridge.BR-LMS-235.summary: Partly covered. The Loan Statement of Account report and its scheduled email work. There is no closure letter, and no message is sent when a loan closes.
bridge.BR-LMS-235.title: Closure letter, final statement and a message

concept.BR-GOV-001.summary: The platform never keeps a money balance, posts to the bank's books or moves money on its own; it sends instructions to the bank's core system and records the replies.
concept.BR-GOV-001.title: The platform never holds money or books entries itself

concept.BR-GOV-002.summary: Each financial instruction the platform sends carries a unique key, so that a repeat can never create a second loan, a second payout or a second posting.
concept.BR-GOV-002.title: Every outgoing instruction carries a unique key

concept.BR-GOV-003.summary: When a call to an outside system fails or times out, the platform does not guess what happened; it asks that system for the real state before any retry or status change.
concept.BR-GOV-003.title: After a failed call, ask the other system before retrying

concept.BR-GOV-004.summary: The platform keeps its own status for every application and loan and compares it with the bank's core system daily; where they differ the core system is right and the difference is an exception to close.
concept.BR-GOV-004.title: The platform's status is checked against the bank's core system every day

concept.BR-GOV-005.summary: Limits, tenors, rates, eligibility rules and similar product behaviour are settings the bank can change, not logic fixed in the program.
concept.BR-GOV-005.title: Product behaviour is set by configuration, not code

concept.BR-GOV-006.summary: Each link to an outside system goes through an adapter, so replacing that system needs a new adapter and leaves the origination and servicing engine untouched.
concept.BR-GOV-006.title: Every outside system sits behind a replaceable adapter

concept.BR-GOV-007.summary: If an outside system is unavailable, the affected step pauses with a clear message and retries by itself, and the platform never fails an application, corrupts a loan or invents a decision.
concept.BR-GOV-007.title: When an outside system is down, the step pauses and retries

concept.BR-GOV-008.summary: Repricing, restructuring, settlement, waiver, write-off, bulk operations and corrective postings each need a second, different person to approve them.
concept.BR-GOV-008.title: Controlled money changes need two different people

concept.BR-GOV-009.summary: Repayment, schedule and accounting histories cannot be changed or deleted; a mistake is fixed by a controlled reversal and a new entry, and the original stays.
concept.BR-GOV-009.title: Financial histories are never overwritten; corrections add entries

concept.BR-GOV-010.summary: Effective date, posting date, value date and the system timestamp are recorded as four different things and are never treated as one.
concept.BR-GOV-010.title: Four kinds of date are kept apart and never mixed

concept.BR-GOV-011.summary: For any application or loan, the platform can show the status it had on a past date and the configuration and rule versions that applied that day.
concept.BR-GOV-011.title: Any past date can be reproduced: status, configuration and rules then in force

concept.BR-GOV-012.summary: The same word means the same thing on every screen, report and extract, and where the bank has its own word for a state, the bank's word is used.
concept.BR-GOV-012.title: One vocabulary across every screen, report and extract

concept.BR-GOV-020.summary: Access is given through roles, one person can hold more than one role, and permissions can be set per function and not only per role.
concept.BR-GOV-020.title: Access follows roles, and a person can hold several

concept.BR-GOV-021.summary: A partner's users can reach only their own organisation's data, and cannot see, work out or export another partner's data by any route, including error messages.
concept.BR-GOV-021.title: A partner's users see only their own partner's data

concept.BR-GOV-022.summary: A person cannot approve their own maker action, and the platform enforces this at the point of approval, not only by hiding a button.
concept.BR-GOV-022.title: Nobody approves their own work, and the system enforces it

concept.BR-GOV-023.summary: A sampling reviewer cannot review an application sent by an organisation their account is linked to, or one they have decided before.
concept.BR-GOV-023.title: A sampling reviewer cannot review their own organisation's or their own earlier cases

concept.BR-GOV-024.summary: Every bank and partner user account must use multi-factor authentication when signing in.
concept.BR-GOV-024.title: Every bank and partner account needs a second login factor

concept.BR-GOV-025.summary: Credit bureau data, identity images, biometrics and a borrower's full financial position need their own permission, and every access is logged with who, which record and when.
concept.BR-GOV-025.title: Sensitive personal data is permissioned apart and every look is logged

concept.BR-GOV-026.summary: User accounts are disabled automatically after a set time without use, and immediately when the bank's HR process says so.
concept.BR-GOV-026.title: Idle accounts switch off, and so do accounts the HR process ends

concept.BR-GOV-027.summary: Every sign-in attempt, permission change and privileged data access is logged with who, when, from where and what the result was.
concept.BR-GOV-027.title: Sign-ins, permission changes and sensitive views are logged with source and outcome

concept.BR-GOV-028.summary: Limits for score override, sampling override, sanction and sanction variation, waiver, settlement, write-off and rate change can be set by role and amount band, are enforced when the action is taken, and a case above a user's limit goes up to someone else.
concept.BR-GOV-028.title: Approval limits by role and amount, and a case over the limit escalates

concept.BR-GOV-030.summary: Every day the platform compares confirmed payouts recorded in origination with loans booked in servicing, and every difference in either direction becomes an exception to be closed with a written reason.
concept.BR-GOV-030.title: A daily check compares payouts in origination with loans in servicing

concept.BR-GOV-031.summary: The bank's existing loans are moved into servicing through a controlled opening-balance load with principal, interest, penalty and charge balances, source references, control-total reconciliation and formal sign-off before go-live.
concept.BR-GOV-031.title: The existing loan book moves in through a controlled opening-balance load

concept.BR-GOV-040.summary: A change to a regulatory rule is made as a versioned, effective-dated configuration change, and returns for earlier periods keep the rules in force in those periods.
concept.BR-GOV-040.title: A changed regulatory rule takes effect from a date and leaves past returns alone

concept.BR-GOV-050.summary: Every day the platform compares its own application and loan status with the core banking system for each record after approval, and produces an exception report of all differences.
concept.BR-GOV-050.title: A daily comparison of the platform and the core banking system

concept.BR-GOV-051.summary: Reconciliation finds, as a minimum, five kinds of difference: loans booked outside the platform, loans approved but absent externally, amount mismatches, status divergence and orphaned idempotency keys.
concept.BR-GOV-051.title: What the daily comparison must find

concept.BR-GOV-052.summary: Each reconciliation break can be assigned to an owner and needs a documented closure; open breaks age visibly and are reported to management after a configurable period.
concept.BR-GOV-052.title: Each difference has an owner, a documented closure, and ages visibly

concept.BR-GOV-053.summary: The platform reconciles internally across schedule, demand, accrual, repayment allocation and accounting posting, and reports any inconsistency as an exception.
concept.BR-GOV-053.title: The platform checks its own records against each other

concept.BR-GOV-054.summary: Every reconciliation run and every closure record is retained in the immutable audit trail.
concept.BR-GOV-054.title: Reconciliation runs and closures are kept in the audit trail

concept.BR-INT-001.summary: The platform obtains an account's existence, status, product type, title, CIF reference and KYC currency from the core banking system.
concept.BR-INT-001.title: Look up an account in the core banking system

concept.BR-INT-002.summary: Account enquiries are queued at a throughput agreed at design stage; if a same-day batch cannot be checked fast enough, the bank and supplier agree more automation capacity or an offline file.
concept.BR-INT-002.title: Account lookups are queued, with an agreed rate or an offline file

concept.BR-INT-003.summary: The platform opens a loan account in the core banking system with the borrower reference, product code and sanctioned terms, and keeps the loan account number the system shows.
concept.BR-INT-003.title: Open the loan account in the core banking system and keep its number

concept.BR-INT-004.summary: The platform disburses against an opened loan account to the validated target account, and keeps the transaction reference and value date the core banking system records.
concept.BR-INT-004.title: Pay out against the opened account and keep the reference and date

concept.BR-INT-005.summary: Every instruction carries a platform-made unique reference written into a durable field of the core banking system record, so the platform can later tell whether it ran.
concept.BR-INT-005.title: Every instruction carries a unique reference the bank's record keeps

concept.BR-INT-006.summary: Because the core banking system cannot recognise a repeated instruction, the platform checks the state first, runs the instruction with its reference, verifies afterwards and blocks on any doubt.
concept.BR-INT-006.title: A compensating control stands in for idempotency

concept.BR-INT-007.summary: The platform records approved demand, accrual, charge, restructure, settlement and write-off accounting effects in the core banking system and keeps the voucher or journal reference.
concept.BR-INT-007.title: Post the accounting effects to the core banking system and keep the reference

concept.BR-INT-008.summary: The platform can raise a controlled reversal of a prior transaction, keeping the original, recording the new reference, and handing a task to a human authoriser where the bank needs one.
concept.BR-INT-008.title: Raise a controlled reversal of an earlier transaction

concept.BR-INT-009.summary: The platform retrieves account statement, balance and loan account status, by a scheduled extract where live retrieval is impractical at volume.
concept.BR-INT-009.title: Retrieve statement, balance and loan account status from the core banking system

concept.BR-INT-010.summary: Where an instruction fails, is interrupted or gives an unrecognised result, the platform re-reads the core banking system for the definitive state before any retry or status change.
concept.BR-INT-010.title: After a failure or odd result, read the real state before trying again

concept.BR-INT-011.summary: Every interaction with the core banking system is logged with request reference, timestamp, initiating user, outcome and duration, with customer details masked and shown unmasked only under privileged access.
concept.BR-INT-011.title: Log every interaction, masking customer details

concept.BR-INT-012.summary: The core banking system is reached through one adapter, so the automation can later be replaced by a real interface without changing the origination or servicing engine.
concept.BR-INT-012.title: Reach the core banking system through a single adapter

concept.BR-INT-020.summary: The handoff of a confirmed funded loan from origination to servicing carries the complete package specified in BR-LOS-010 and is idempotent.
concept.BR-INT-020.title: The handoff to servicing carries the full package and is idempotent

concept.BR-INT-021.summary: Servicing gives origination back the loan account status, sanctioned amount, disbursement date, tenor, instalment amount and arrears position.
concept.BR-INT-021.title: Servicing reports loan status back to origination

concept.BR-INT-022.summary: A failed or rejected handoff raises an exception on both sides, and neither side progresses the loan until the exception is closed.
concept.BR-INT-022.title: A failed handoff stops both sides until the exception is closed

concept.BR-INT-030.summary: A bureau inquiry runs from a designated host inside the bank's permitted network, through robotic process automation driving the bureau interface, under the same controls as section 9.3.
concept.BR-INT-030.title: The bureau inquiry runs from a designated host, through automation, under the same controls

concept.BR-INT-031.summary: The bureau automation is monitored for failure and for interface change, and alerts on consecutive failures rather than degrading silently.
concept.BR-INT-031.title: The bureau automation is monitored and alerts on repeated failure

concept.BR-INT-032.summary: Bureau credentials and session handling are isolated from the main application and from the core banking system automation, and reachable only by the component that needs them.
concept.BR-INT-032.title: Bureau credentials are kept separate from the rest of the system

concept.BR-INT-033.summary: Every bureau inquiry is logged in line with BR-LOS-196 and retained for the full retention period.
concept.BR-INT-033.title: Every bureau inquiry is logged and kept for the retention period

concept.BR-INT-040.summary: The platform verifies each applicant against the Election Commission Database, returning a demographic agreement, a portrait and a verification reference, and keeps the portrait for face comparison.
concept.BR-INT-040.title: Verify each applicant's identity against the Election Commission Database

concept.BR-INT-041.summary: At field verification the platform checks that the applicant is physically present, using liveness detection.
concept.BR-INT-041.title: Check that the applicant is physically present

concept.BR-INT-042.summary: The platform compares the live capture with the retained portrait by face matching and keeps the confidence score against the application.
concept.BR-INT-042.title: Compare the live face with the stored portrait and keep the score

concept.BR-INT-043.summary: Identity images and portraits are encrypted at rest, access-logged, and retained under bank policy.
concept.BR-INT-043.title: Identity images are encrypted, access-logged and retained under bank policy

concept.BR-INT-044.summary: Where identity verification is unavailable, the application holds rather than fails, with automatic retry.
concept.BR-INT-044.title: If identity verification is down, the application waits and retries

concept.BR-INT-050.summary: The platform sends one-time passcodes by SMS for multi-factor authentication.
concept.BR-INT-050.title: Send one-time passcodes by SMS for multi-factor sign-in

concept.BR-INT-051.summary: Borrowers are notified on disbursement, instalment due and overdue, approved term change, settlement and closure, through configurable templates in Bangla and English.
concept.BR-INT-051.title: Borrower notices for five events, in Bangla and English

concept.BR-INT-052.summary: A failed notification is retried and reported, and never blocks or reverses a loan action.
concept.BR-INT-052.title: A failed notification is retried and reported, and never blocks a loan action

concept.BR-INT-053.summary: One-time passcode messages do not include customer, account or loan identifiers; this row is a Should, not a Must.
concept.BR-INT-053.title: Passcode messages carry no customer, account or loan identifiers

concept.BR-INT-054.summary: The notification channels and the full set of borrower notice templates are to be confirmed by the bank.
concept.BR-INT-054.title: The bank confirms the channels and the full set of borrower notices

concept.BR-INT-060.summary: The automation runs only on infrastructure the bank designates inside its network, and never sends core banking system content outside that perimeter.
concept.BR-INT-060.title: The automation runs only inside the bank's network

concept.BR-INT-061.summary: The automation signs in with dedicated service accounts the bank sets up, holding only the privilege its transactions need, and never shared with or used by a person.
concept.BR-INT-061.title: The automation signs in with its own dedicated accounts

concept.BR-INT-062.summary: Credentials are held in a secured credential store, never appear in code, configuration, screenshots or logs, and can be rotated without a software release.
concept.BR-INT-062.title: Credentials sit in a secured store and can be rotated without a release

concept.BR-INT-063.summary: Every automated transaction is attributable to the user or process that started it; the audit trail records both that actor and the service account used.
concept.BR-INT-063.title: Every automated transaction can be traced to who caused it

concept.BR-INT-064.summary: Each automation run keeps evidence of the screens traversed, the values entered and the values read back, enough to reconstruct the transaction for audit or dispute.
concept.BR-INT-064.title: Each automation run keeps evidence of what it did

concept.BR-INT-065.summary: Before entering any value the automation checks it is on the screen it is meant to see; on anything unexpected it aborts the transaction safely, raises an exception and stops.
concept.BR-INT-065.title: On an unexpected screen the automation stops safely

concept.BR-INT-066.summary: The automation is monitored continuously for availability, queue depth, transaction duration, failure rate and interface change, and alerts on consecutive failures.
concept.BR-INT-066.title: The automation is monitored and alerts on repeated failure

concept.BR-INT-067.summary: The platform presents an operations view of pending, in progress, completed and failed automation transactions, where an item can be retried, cancelled or escalated under maker-checker.
concept.BR-INT-067.title: An operations view of automation work, with controlled retry, cancel and escalate

concept.BR-INT-068.summary: Automation capacity scales sideways: extra concurrent sessions raise throughput without change to the origination or servicing engine, within the core banking system's own limits.
concept.BR-INT-068.title: More automation sessions add throughput without changing the engine

concept.BR-INT-069.summary: When the automation is unavailable the affected step pauses with a clear message and retries by itself; it never fails an application, corrupts a loan's state or invents an outcome.
concept.BR-INT-069.title: When the automation is down, the step pauses and retries

concept.BR-INT-070.summary: Every automated transaction has a manual fallback: authorised bank staff can do it directly in the core banking system and record its reference, so a long outage does not halt lending.
concept.BR-INT-070.title: A manual fallback for every automated transaction

concept.BR-INT-071.summary: The automation is re-validated in a representative test environment before any core banking system change reaches production, and the bank gives advance notice of such changes.
concept.BR-INT-071.title: Re-test the automation before any change to the core banking system

concept.BR-INT-072.summary: Daily reconciliation compares every instruction the platform believes it issued with the transactions present in the core banking system, in both directions, and raises each difference as an exception.
concept.BR-INT-072.title: The daily reconciliation checks every instruction in both directions

concept.BR-LMS-001.summary: Every loan has exactly one current servicing status at a time, and the platform keeps the whole history of earlier statuses with the date and reason for each change.
concept.BR-LMS-001.title: A loan has exactly one current status, with its full history

concept.BR-LMS-002.summary: Changing a loan's status never deletes or overwrites an earlier classification, schedule version or posting; older records are kept and marked as superseded.
concept.BR-LMS-002.title: A status change never erases or overwrites earlier records

concept.BR-LMS-003.summary: The names of servicing statuses are aligned with the bank's existing vocabulary and with Bangladesh Bank classification terms before the configuration is fixed.
concept.BR-LMS-003.title: Status names follow the bank's own words and Bangladesh Bank's

concept.BR-LMS-010.summary: Servicing takes a loan only when the handoff is complete and carries a confirmed payout reference; any other handoff is rejected to an exception queue with a reason and creates no loan.
concept.BR-LMS-010.title: Servicing accepts only a complete, confirmed handoff; others go to an exception queue

concept.BR-LMS-011.summary: A repeated handoff for the same origination reference returns the original loan and never creates a second one.
concept.BR-LMS-011.title: Sending the same handoff twice never creates a second loan

concept.BR-LMS-100.summary: The loan system takes on a loan only when it arrives confirmed as paid out, with its approved terms, its payout reference and the record of who approved it.
concept.BR-LMS-100.title: Accept only loans that are really paid out

concept.BR-LMS-101.summary: Every loan has one place where staff can find the borrower, product, terms, balances, repayment plan, bills, payments, accounting entries, grade and history.
concept.BR-LMS-101.title: One record holds everything about a loan

concept.BR-LMS-102.summary: A loan moves from booked to active, sometimes through partially disbursed, then to closure requested and finally to closed, settled or written off. Servicing starts only after the money is paid out.
concept.BR-LMS-102.title: The stages of a loan's life

concept.BR-LMS-103.summary: A loan product is a template. Schedule method, rate, charges and accounting mappings come from it, so staff do not type them again on every loan.
concept.BR-LMS-103.title: Rules come from the product, not from each loan

concept.BR-LMS-104.summary: Where the bank approves a limit larger than the amount paid out, the loan system remembers the approved limit and shows how much of it is used.
concept.BR-LMS-104.title: Track the approved limit separately from what was taken

concept.BR-LMS-105.summary: On go-live the bank's current loans move over with their balances and a reference to the old record, and the totals are checked against the old system before the loans start running.
concept.BR-LMS-105.title: Bring existing loans over from the old system, and prove the totals match

concept.BR-LMS-106.summary: Every loan carries a label such as Retail, SME or Agriculture so that management and regulatory reports can group loans.
concept.BR-LMS-106.title: Each loan has a category for reports

concept.BR-LMS-110.summary: The bank needs at least five repayment methods: equal monthly instalments, pro-rated, fixed cycle date, flat interest and a revolving line of credit.
concept.BR-LMS-110.title: Five ways of working out repayments

concept.BR-LMS-111.summary: For each product the loan system stores the rate, the calculation method and the rate type. A floating product also stores how often the rate is reviewed and which reference rate it follows.
concept.BR-LMS-111.title: Store the interest rate, how it is calculated, and whether it is fixed or floating

concept.BR-LMS-112.summary: A moratorium is a payment holiday, usually at the start of a loan. The product must say how long it lasts and what happens to principal and interest during it.
concept.BR-LMS-112.title: Payment holiday (moratorium) rules

concept.BR-LMS-113.summary: Each fee has rules for when it applies, how it is calculated and which accounts it goes to when it is billed, earned, forgiven or written off.
concept.BR-LMS-113.title: Rules for fees and charges

concept.BR-LMS-114.summary: When a borrower pays, the system must decide which debt the money clears first: charges, penalty, interest or principal. The bank wants a different order for healthy, bad, written-off and settled loans.
concept.BR-LMS-114.title: The order in which a payment is used

concept.BR-LMS-115.summary: The bank must choose whether the loan system keeps its own accounts and posts to the general ledger, or only works out what borrowers owe while the CBS keeps the official accounts.
concept.BR-LMS-115.title: Two ways of keeping the accounts

concept.BR-LMS-116.summary: Where a product is funded together with another lender, the product records which partners take part and what share each one funds.
concept.BR-LMS-116.title: Link co-lending partners to the product

concept.BR-LMS-117.summary: Product rules must never change silently. Each change gets a version and a start date and needs a second person to approve it, and each loan remembers the version it was booked under.
concept.BR-LMS-117.title: Product rules have versions, start dates and approval

concept.BR-LMS-120.summary: When a funded loan is booked, the system builds its first repayment plan from the amount, rate, term, dates, payment frequency and any payment holiday.
concept.BR-LMS-120.title: Build the first repayment plan

concept.BR-LMS-121.summary: Every line of the repayment plan shows the instalment and how much of it is principal and how much is interest, with the balance left after it.
concept.BR-LMS-121.title: Each row shows the split

concept.BR-LMS-122.summary: When a loan is paid out in stages, the repayment plan is rebuilt or adjusted each time a part is released, following the approved tranche rules.
concept.BR-LMS-122.title: Rebuild the plan when money is paid out in parts

concept.BR-LMS-123.summary: When a loan is co-lent, the system keeps a second repayment plan for the partner's share, alongside the borrower's plan.
concept.BR-LMS-123.title: Keep a partner's plan for co-lent loans

concept.BR-LMS-124.summary: Staff can show a borrower the effect of a proposed change on screen before it is committed, and nothing is posted or saved.
concept.BR-LMS-124.title: "What-if" view with nothing saved

concept.BR-LMS-125.summary: When a repayment plan is replaced, the old one is kept as a superseded version, linked to the new plan and to the event that caused the change.
concept.BR-LMS-125.title: Never overwrite an old plan

concept.BR-LMS-126.summary: A repayment plan may be rebuilt only because of an approved change, and the new plan records the reason.
concept.BR-LMS-126.title: Only an approved change may rebuild a plan

concept.BR-LMS-130.summary: On each due date the system raises a bill (a demand) for the instalment and its parts: principal, interest, penalty, charges and broken-period interest.
concept.BR-LMS-130.title: Raise the bills on their due dates

concept.BR-LMS-131.summary: The bank can attach product fees, repayment fees, prepayment fees, restructuring fees and approved one-off fees to a loan as configured.
concept.BR-LMS-131.title: Attach fees to the loan

concept.BR-LMS-132.summary: Staff can see, for any date, what a loan owes in overdue and current amounts by component, without posting anything.
concept.BR-LMS-132.title: "What is owed on this date" view

concept.BR-LMS-133.summary: A bill is never silently deleted or changed. A correction is a controlled reversal with a reason and an approver, and the original and the reversal both stay visible.
concept.BR-LMS-133.title: Never delete or quietly change a bill

concept.BR-LMS-134.summary: Where the CBS keeps the ledger, the loan system sends it each bill and its accounting effect, and keeps the CBS journal number against the loan.
concept.BR-LMS-134.title: Send bills to the CBS and keep its journal number

concept.BR-LMS-135.summary: Raising bills for all loans is a batch that gives a result for each loan, so a partial failure can be finished without redoing the loans already done.
concept.BR-LMS-135.title: Bill-raising runs as a batch that can restart

concept.BR-LMS-140.summary: The system counts normal interest as it builds up, following the product's accrual frequency and using the balance, rate, day-count convention and dates.
concept.BR-LMS-140.title: Count interest every day (accrual)

concept.BR-LMS-141.summary: Interest charged on overdue amounts (penal interest) is calculated and tracked apart from normal interest, at a rate and on a basis that can be configured.
concept.BR-LMS-141.title: Penalty interest, kept separate

concept.BR-LMS-142.summary: When a partial period arises at payout, at a change of terms or at closure, the interest for those odd days is handled and charged.
concept.BR-LMS-142.title: Interest for odd days (broken period)

concept.BR-LMS-143.summary: Where a correction is needed, interest for a date range can be reversed and posted again for many loans, with approval, and the reversed entries stay visible.
concept.BR-LMS-143.title: Undo and redo interest for a period, with approval

concept.BR-LMS-144.summary: When a loan becomes non-performing, interest and charges that are unpaid stop counting as income and move to a suspense account.
concept.BR-LMS-144.title: Stop counting interest as income on bad loans

concept.BR-LMS-145.summary: The system compares the interest in the plan, the bills, the accruals, the collected income and the ledger, and reports every difference.
concept.BR-LMS-145.title: Check that interest numbers agree everywhere

concept.BR-LMS-150.summary: Staff can select the loans to reprice by product, customer segment, branch or loan number, limited to active floating-rate loans.
concept.BR-LMS-150.title: Choose which loans to reprice

concept.BR-LMS-151.summary: A repricing takes effect on an approved date: the old rate applies up to it and the new rate from it.
concept.BR-LMS-151.title: The new rate starts on a set date

concept.BR-LMS-152.summary: Repricing never rewrites paid instalments, completed repayments or posted history. Only the outstanding principal and unpaid instalments are recalculated.
concept.BR-LMS-152.title: Never change what is already paid

concept.BR-LMS-153.summary: A repricing can either keep the end date and revise the instalment, or keep the instalment and revise the term.
