concept.BR-LMS-153.title: Two repricing options

concept.BR-LMS-154.summary: Before a repricing is run for real, a dry run shows each loan's old and new figures, every failure and every excluded loan with its reason.
concept.BR-LMS-154.title: A practice run first

concept.BR-LMS-155.summary: A repricing run needs two people: a maker creates it and an independent checker approves it before any loan is changed.
concept.BR-LMS-155.title: One person prepares, another approves

concept.BR-LMS-156.summary: Each repriced loan receives a new schedule version, and the earlier version and the relationship between them are kept.
concept.BR-LMS-156.title: Each repriced loan gets a new plan version

concept.BR-LMS-157.summary: The repricing batch can be run again safely: it is idempotent, works loan by loan, can be resumed, and records a status for each row.
concept.BR-LMS-157.title: The repricing batch is safe to run and rerun

concept.BR-LMS-158.summary: Fixed-rate, closed, written-off, frozen and other ineligible loans are left out automatically, and the reason is recorded.
concept.BR-LMS-158.title: Skip loans that shouldn't be repriced, automatically

concept.BR-LMS-159.summary: After a repricing is approved and active, the affected borrowers are told through the configured notification channel.
concept.BR-LMS-159.title: Tell the borrowers

concept.BR-LMS-160.summary: Every repayment is stored with its channel, its CBS reference, the amount and two dates: when the money really arrived and when staff entered it.
concept.BR-LMS-160.title: Record a confirmed payment with full details

concept.BR-LMS-161.summary: A payment that is started but not confirmed by the CBS must never reduce what the borrower owes, and must show as pending, not paid.
concept.BR-LMS-161.title: A payment counts only after the CBS confirms it

concept.BR-LMS-162.summary: The same payment must never be counted twice, however many times the loan system hears about it. The CBS transaction reference is the key.
concept.BR-LMS-162.title: Apply each payment only once

concept.BR-LMS-163.summary: A payment is applied as at its value date. Days past due, penalty and grade are recalculated as of that date, so a borrower is never punished for the bank's own delay.
concept.BR-LMS-163.title: Use the date the money actually arrived

concept.BR-LMS-164.summary: A payment is split across what is owed in an order the bank sets, and the split is shown line by line on the loan.
concept.BR-LMS-164.title: Split the payment in the set order and show it

concept.BR-LMS-165.summary: The loan system must handle nine kinds of money movement against a loan, from a normal instalment to a recovery after a write-off.
concept.BR-LMS-165.title: All the payment types the bank needs

concept.BR-LMS-166.summary: Many payments can be loaded from one file. Every row is checked before anything posts, each row reports success or failure, and a stopped upload can continue.
concept.BR-LMS-166.title: Upload many payments in one file

concept.BR-LMS-167.summary: Money that cannot be matched to a loan waits in an unidentified-receipts queue with an owner and an age, and does not reduce anyone's balance until it is matched.
concept.BR-LMS-167.title: Money nobody can match goes to a queue

concept.BR-LMS-168.summary: The system must be able to say, at any moment, the exact amount that would close a loan today, and support approved partial and full settlements against it.
concept.BR-LMS-168.title: How much to close today?

concept.BR-LMS-169.summary: When payments were posted wrongly, they are reprocessed through a controlled, approved, restartable repost that keeps the original entries.
concept.BR-LMS-169.title: Fix wrong payment postings safely

concept.BR-LMS-170c.summary: The platform keeps a master list of the security behind loans: type, description, valuation, price history, the haircut that applies and the resulting eligible value.
concept.BR-LMS-170c.title: A master list of collateral

concept.BR-LMS-170r.summary: If someone records or reverses a payment directly in the CBS without the loan system knowing, reconciliation must find it, raise an exception and fix it by a controlled repost.
concept.BR-LMS-170r.title: Catch payments made directly in the CBS

concept.BR-LMS-171c.summary: A pledge moves through set steps from pledge requested to pledged, then release requested and released, repossessed or cancelled, and every step is authorised and recorded.
concept.BR-LMS-171c.title: The life of a pledge

concept.BR-LMS-171r.summary: For every payment the system checks that the CBS reference, the way the money was split and the accounting entry all agree, and reports anything that does not.
concept.BR-LMS-171r.title: Match every payment end to end

concept.BR-LMS-172.summary: The platform compares the value of the collateral with the amount lent, on a schedule and on demand, and flags the gap when the collateral no longer covers the loan.
concept.BR-LMS-172.title: Watch for a collateral shortfall

concept.BR-LMS-173.summary: When there is a shortfall, the platform tracks the remedy (more security, a repayment or an approved exception), each with an owner and a due date.
concept.BR-LMS-173.title: Track how a shortfall is fixed

concept.BR-LMS-174.summary: Security may be given back only after the platform checks that the loan is still covered and someone approves the release.
concept.BR-LMS-174.title: Release collateral only after checks and approval

concept.BR-LMS-175.summary: The platform reports collateral exposure by borrower and in total, a ledger of every collateral event, and the current status of every pledged item.
concept.BR-LMS-175.title: Collateral reports

concept.BR-LMS-180.summary: When a borrower pays ahead of the due dates, the money is applied to the coming instalments in the way the loan product says.
concept.BR-LMS-180.title: Paying future EMIs early (advance payment)

concept.BR-LMS-181.summary: A prepayment lowers the principal early and may carry a fee. After it, either the instalment falls or the loan ends sooner, as the borrower chooses and the bank approves.
concept.BR-LMS-181.title: Paying extra to cut the loan (prepayment)

concept.BR-LMS-182.summary: The platform can change the terms of a loan for a borrower who cannot keep up, by moving dates or the term or by changing the money terms, and it records what kind of change it was.
concept.BR-LMS-182.title: Changing the terms for a struggling borrower (restructuring)

concept.BR-LMS-183.summary: A restructure produces a new repayment plan, and the old plan is kept and marked as restructured and replaced.
concept.BR-LMS-183.title: A restructure makes a new plan and keeps the old one

concept.BR-LMS-184.summary: Each branch can restructure only up to a set share of its loans in a period, and the platform keeps a log of how much of the limit has been used.
concept.BR-LMS-184.title: Limits on how much can be restructured

concept.BR-LMS-185.summary: A manual change to what a borrower owes (a waiver, capitalising interest, carrying an amount forward, or correcting a balance) needs a second person to approve it and must record the amount before and after, the reason, the approver and a reference.
concept.BR-LMS-185.title: Manual corrections need two people and a full record

concept.BR-LMS-186.summary: If a borrower has paid too much, the extra can be refunded after approval, and the refund is recorded on the loan with its bank reference.
concept.BR-LMS-186.title: Refund overpayments, with approval

concept.BR-LMS-187.summary: Where a product keeps a cash deposit from the borrower as a guarantee, the platform tracks when it was received, how much was used, how much is left, and the refund.
concept.BR-LMS-187.title: Track a security deposit

concept.BR-LMS-188.summary: Every restructure, reschedule and waiver must be reported to Bangladesh Bank and given the classification treatment its rules require, and the platform records which treatment it applied.
concept.BR-LMS-188.title: Report restructures and waivers to Bangladesh Bank

concept.BR-LMS-190.summary: Every day the platform works out how many days late each loan is, from its unpaid bills, and keeps that day's figure on record.
concept.BR-LMS-190.title: Count days late every day, and keep the history

concept.BR-LMS-191.summary: Each loan gets a grade from how many days late it is, and an authorised person can override the grade by hand, with a reason and an approver.
concept.BR-LMS-191.title: Give each loan a health grade

concept.BR-LMS-192.summary: Every move into or out of the early-warning and bad-loan grades is kept as history, and a past grade is never deleted.
concept.BR-LMS-192.title: Keep the history of grade changes

concept.BR-LMS-193.summary: The platform works out how much the bank must set aside against loans that may not be repaid. The rate depends on the grade and on whether the loan is secured, semi-secured or unsecured, and the basis of each calculation is kept.
concept.BR-LMS-193.title: Set money aside for expected losses (provisioning)

concept.BR-LMS-194.summary: After a loan turns bad, its unpaid interest and charges are moved to a holding account called suspense, and go back to income only when the money is actually collected.
concept.BR-LMS-194.title: Unpaid interest waits in suspense

concept.BR-LMS-195.summary: The point at which a loan may be written off is set by its own threshold, separate from the grade bands.
concept.BR-LMS-195.title: Write-off has its own trigger

concept.BR-LMS-196.summary: Some events stop normal processing, such as a borrower's death or a court order. The platform records the freeze and unfreeze dates, exactly what was stopped, and who authorised it.
concept.BR-LMS-196.title: Freezing a loan

concept.BR-LMS-197.summary: The rules for grade bands, provision percentages and income treatment belong to Credit Risk and Finance. They are versioned, dated and approved by a second person, and every grade or provision records which version of the rules it used.
concept.BR-LMS-197.title: Grade, provision and income rules are owned and versioned

concept.BR-LMS-198.summary: Late loans enter a collections process: a record of every contact, promises to pay and whether they were kept, follow-up dates, and escalation to recovery or legal action.
concept.BR-LMS-198.title: Chasing late payers (collections)

concept.BR-LMS-200.summary: When the bank agrees to accept less than the full amount to close a loan, the platform shows what makes up the figure (principal, interest, penalties, charges and the waivers) before anyone approves it.
concept.BR-LMS-200.title: Work out a settlement offer and show its make-up

concept.BR-LMS-201.summary: Settlements, waivers and write-offs need a second person's approval, and who may approve depends on the amount and on the person's role.
concept.BR-LMS-201.title: Approval limits for settlements, waivers and write-offs

concept.BR-LMS-202.summary: A write-off takes the expected loss off the bank's books, but the loan, its repayment plans, its payments and its grade history must stay fully viewable.
concept.BR-LMS-202.title: A write-off keeps the history

concept.BR-LMS-203.summary: Money collected later on a loan that was written off is recorded as a write-off recovery on the original loan and treated according to the bank's policy.
concept.BR-LMS-203.title: Money collected after a write-off

concept.BR-LMS-204.summary: The accounting for settlements, write-offs and recoveries goes to the bank's core banking system (CBS), and the journal number the CBS returns is kept on the record.
concept.BR-LMS-204.title: Send settlements and write-offs to the CBS

concept.BR-LMS-205.summary: Each settlement, waiver, write-off and recovery keeps the amounts before and after, the reason, the person who made it, the person who approved it, the approval date and any external reference.
concept.BR-LMS-205.title: Full record for every settlement, waiver, write-off and recovery

concept.BR-LMS-210.summary: The platform keeps a list of co-lending partners with their details, their addresses and the kind of risk-sharing arrangement in force, such as a first-loss default guarantee.
concept.BR-LMS-210.title: A list of co-lending partners

concept.BR-LMS-211.summary: For each partner the platform defines the products it takes part in, its share of the lending and its share of the collections.
concept.BR-LMS-211.title: Which products each partner joins, and its share

concept.BR-LMS-212.summary: The platform works out the partner's share of every repayment plan and shares one-off charges with the partner as agreed.
concept.BR-LMS-212.title: The partner's share of each plan and of charges

concept.BR-LMS-213.summary: The platform processes partner credit notes and checks the partner's position on a regular cycle, reporting anything that does not match.
concept.BR-LMS-213.title: Partner settlements and checks

concept.BR-LMS-214.summary: Reports for each partner show the share paid out, the share collected, the share still owed, the late loans in the partner's portfolio and how much of the guarantee has been used.
concept.BR-LMS-214.title: Partner reports

concept.BR-LMS-220.summary: Loans can be moved from one branch to another in bulk, and each loan keeps its own record and its full history.
concept.BR-LMS-220.title: Move loans between branches in bulk

concept.BR-LMS-221.summary: For credit lines, the platform tracks the maximum, used and available limit, and logs every change to the limit with its reason and its approver.
concept.BR-LMS-221.title: Credit-line limits and their change log

concept.BR-LMS-222.summary: Credit lines that are fully repaid are closed by a scheduled job, as the product is set up to do.
concept.BR-LMS-222.title: Close repaid credit lines automatically

concept.BR-LMS-223.summary: Every batch job (interest, bills, grades, uploads) shows a clear state and a result for each row, and can be restarted without posting anything twice.
concept.BR-LMS-223.title: Every batch has a clear status

concept.BR-LMS-224.summary: Failed bills, failed payments, failed postings, failed connections and unmatched items each appear in a work queue with an owner, an age and a written note when they are closed.
concept.BR-LMS-224.title: Work queues for things that went wrong

concept.BR-LMS-225.summary: Scheduled jobs and connections are monitored. When one fails, or fails several times in a row, someone is alerted, and nothing is allowed to fail silently.
concept.BR-LMS-225.title: Alerts when jobs fail

concept.BR-LMS-230.summary: Before a loan closes, the system checks that principal, interest, penalty, charges and every other amount are paid or formally settled, and says what is blocking the closure.
concept.BR-LMS-230.title: Check everything is cleared before closing

concept.BR-LMS-231.summary: When the core banking system (CBS) keeps the books, the loan system checks the loan account and ledger in the CBS before it confirms the closure.
concept.BR-LMS-231.title: Check the core bank before confirming closure

concept.BR-LMS-232.summary: At closure, collateral is released after approval, and the release is recorded in the collateral ledger.
concept.BR-LMS-232.title: Release collateral at closure

concept.BR-LMS-233.summary: Any remaining security deposit or overpayment is refunded to the borrower, and the refund is recorded with its bank reference.
concept.BR-LMS-233.title: Refund what is left

concept.BR-LMS-234.summary: Closure follows an authorised path from closure requested to closed, and keeps who authorised it and when.
concept.BR-LMS-234.title: Closure needs approval

concept.BR-LMS-235.summary: At closure the borrower gets a payoff or closure letter, a final statement of account and a message through the agreed channel.
concept.BR-LMS-235.title: Closure letter, final statement and a message

concept.BR-LMS-240.summary: The platform presents a servicing dashboard of book size and composition, collections against demand, DPD distribution, classification movement, provision position and exception queues.
concept.BR-LMS-240.title: A servicing dashboard shows the state of the loan book

concept.BR-LMS-241.summary: Every report states the date and time it was generated, the parameters used and the data cut-off applied.
concept.BR-LMS-241.title: Every report states when and how it was produced

concept.BR-LMS-242.summary: Servicing reports can be exported to XLSX and CSV, run on a schedule, and delivered to chosen recipients.
concept.BR-LMS-242.title: Servicing reports can be exported, scheduled and sent

concept.BR-LMS-250.summary: The platform produces the monthly CIB contribution extract, with every field Bangladesh Bank requires for each reportable loan; the bank is to supply the format.
concept.BR-LMS-250.title: A monthly extract for the Credit Information Bureau

concept.BR-LMS-251.summary: The platform produces the classification and provisioning returns Bangladesh Bank prescribes, from the same records that drive the bank's internal position.
concept.BR-LMS-251.title: Classification and provisioning returns for Bangladesh Bank

concept.BR-LMS-252.summary: The platform keeps every regulatory extract it generates, with its parameters and the generating user, for the full retention period, so a submitted return can be reproduced exactly.
concept.BR-LMS-252.title: Every regulatory extract is kept so a return can be reproduced

concept.BR-LOS-001.summary: A status change that the lifecycle model does not allow is rejected, logged as an exception, and leaves the application unchanged.
concept.BR-LOS-001.title: Only allowed status changes go through; others are refused and logged

concept.BR-LOS-002.summary: If the sanctioned amount is below the amount requested, both figures are kept, a limit-revised flag is carried, and bank staff, the partner and the field officer can all see both.
concept.BR-LOS-002.title: When less is sanctioned than asked, both amounts are kept and shown

concept.BR-LOS-002a.summary: The servicing system never sets a sanction; the origination system is the sanctioning authority, either by a system decision within set limits or through a credit approver within delegated authority.
concept.BR-LOS-002a.title: Only the origination system sanctions, never the servicing system

concept.BR-LOS-003.summary: An application that stays too long in any status that is not final moves to EXPIRED by itself, after a period the bank sets.
concept.BR-LOS-003.title: Idle applications expire automatically

concept.BR-LOS-004.summary: Each status change writes an audit record that cannot be altered and shows the application, old and new status, who or what made the change, when, and the reason.
concept.BR-LOS-004.title: Every status change leaves a permanent audit record

concept.BR-LOS-010.summary: When a payout is confirmed, the origination system sends the funded loan to servicing as one complete package with the borrower, terms, payout details, collateral and audit reference.
concept.BR-LOS-010.title: One complete handoff package goes to servicing when a loan is paid out

concept.BR-LOS-100.summary: The Bank can onboard a partner organisation and record its legal name, licence and tax numbers, address, contacts, agreement, permitted products, batch and exposure limits and status.
concept.BR-LOS-100.title: A partner organisation is recorded with its legal and commercial details

concept.BR-LOS-101.summary: Every pairing of a partner and a product carries its own ticket size range, tenors, rate and fees, required application fields and optional sampling rate override.
concept.BR-LOS-101.title: Each partner and product pair has its own limits, rates and fields

concept.BR-LOS-102.summary: When a partner is suspended, its users can still read existing applications but cannot submit new batches; applications in progress carry on unless someone halts them.
concept.BR-LOS-102.title: A suspended partner can look but not send new batches

concept.BR-LOS-103.summary: The platform keeps a running total of each partner's exposure against its agreed ceiling, stops a submission that would go over, and tells the partner how much room is left.
concept.BR-LOS-103.title: A submission that would break the partner's exposure ceiling is stopped

concept.BR-LOS-104.summary: Partner administrators can create, suspend and remove users inside their own organisation only, up to a maximum number of users set by the Bank.
concept.BR-LOS-104.title: Partner administrators manage only their own organisation's users

concept.BR-LOS-105.summary: For each partner, the platform records any first-loss default guarantee or other risk-sharing terms and gives them to servicing for partner economics.
concept.BR-LOS-105.title: A partner's first-loss guarantee terms are recorded for servicing to use

concept.BR-LOS-106.summary: The Bank sees each partner's submission volume, validation failure rate, sampling rejection rate, disbursement conversion and, where servicing can supply it, arrears performance on a single record.
concept.BR-LOS-106.title: Partner performance is visible on one partner record

concept.BR-LOS-110.summary: Partners send applications as a CSV or XLSX file in a template issued by the platform, downloadable from the upload screen, versioned, with the version recorded against each batch.
concept.BR-LOS-110.title: Applications come in as a versioned CSV or XLSX template

concept.BR-LOS-111.summary: If a partner's application file has the wrong format, wrong columns or too many rows, the whole file is refused with a clear reason, and nothing from it is loaded.
concept.BR-LOS-111.title: A bad upload file is rejected whole

concept.BR-LOS-112.summary: The upload screen states the file size limit and the row count limit up front, so the partner does not learn them only from an error.
concept.BR-LOS-112.title: File size and row limits are shown before upload

concept.BR-LOS-113.summary: Each row is validated, results are shown as valid, invalid-and-correctable, and duplicate, and every error names the field and gives a reason the partner can act on.
concept.BR-LOS-113.title: Every row is checked and results are sorted into three groups

concept.BR-LOS-114.summary: Invalid rows can be edited in the browser, re-checked one by one without re-uploading the batch, and exported as a corrections file for offline handling.
concept.BR-LOS-114.title: Wrong rows can be fixed in the browser or exported for offline correction

concept.BR-LOS-115.summary: A partner can submit only the valid part of a batch and keep the rest for correction, and gets a confirmation with the row count, total requested value and exposure against the ceiling.
concept.BR-LOS-115.title: The partner can submit the valid rows and keep the rest, with a confirmation summary

concept.BR-LOS-116.summary: Duplicates are looked for within the uploaded batch, against the partner's earlier batches and across all partners, each treated differently.
concept.BR-LOS-116.title: Duplicates are caught at three levels, each with its own treatment

concept.BR-LOS-117.summary: The platform accepts no application without a recorded consent covering data sharing with the Bank, a credit bureau inquiry and identity verification, with the reference, method and time kept for Bank compliance.
concept.BR-LOS-117.title: No application is accepted without recorded borrower consent

concept.BR-LOS-120.summary: Before an application reaches submitted status, the account must pass a check against the bank's core system: it is found, is active, has a permitted type, carries the applicant's name and the customer's KYC is current.
concept.BR-LOS-120.title: No application is submitted without a successful bank account check

concept.BR-LOS-121.summary: Before scoring, names are normalised by case folding, removing titles such as Md., Mohammad, Mst. and Begum, and collapsing spaces; the similarity threshold is configurable and defaults to requiring identical names after normalisation.
concept.BR-LOS-121.title: Names are tidied before they are compared with the account title

concept.BR-LOS-122.summary: An account number may hold only one non-terminal application across the whole platform, whichever partner sent it.
concept.BR-LOS-122.title: One account number can have only one open application anywhere

concept.BR-LOS-123.summary: A validation result expires after a configurable period, seven days by default, and a stale result forces a new check before submission.
concept.BR-LOS-123.title: An account check result expires after a set time

concept.BR-LOS-124.summary: Validation is repeated immediately before the disbursement instruction is sent; an account that has become dormant, closed or otherwise ineligible halts the payout and raises an exception.
concept.BR-LOS-124.title: The account is checked again just before the payout

concept.BR-LOS-125.summary: When the core system or the automation session is unavailable, affected rows are held pending and retried on a schedule; the partner is told validation is in progress, need not re-upload, and a timeout is never recorded as a pass.
concept.BR-LOS-125.title: If the bank's system is down, rows wait and retry; a timeout is never a pass

concept.BR-LOS-126.summary: Validation runs as a queued background process; the partner sees progress, an estimated finish time and each row's state, can leave and return, and is notified when the batch finishes.
concept.BR-LOS-126.title: Account checks run in the background and show progress

concept.BR-LOS-127.summary: Validation requests are queued and rate-limited to what the core system and the automation can sustain, and a long queue is never shown to the partner as an error.
concept.BR-LOS-127.title: Check requests are queued and paced to what the bank's system can take

concept.BR-LOS-130.summary: Once applications are scored, the platform picks a share for manual review at a configured rate, plus every referred or mandatory-sampling case, and passes the rest automatically.
concept.BR-LOS-130.title: After scoring, a share of applications is picked for manual review

concept.BR-LOS-131.summary: Selection uses a cryptographically sound random source; a predictable or sequence-based pick is not acceptable.
concept.BR-LOS-131.title: The random pick must use a sound random source

concept.BR-LOS-132.summary: The selection seed and the rate applied are recorded against the batch so the pick can be independently reproduced and shown to audit at any later date.
concept.BR-LOS-132.title: The seed and rate are saved so a pick can be reproduced for audit

concept.BR-LOS-133.summary: The effective sampling rate is the product-level override if there is one, otherwise the partner-level override, otherwise the global default; a rate change never alters a batch that has been sampled.
concept.BR-LOS-133.title: The sampling rate comes from product, then partner, then global default

concept.BR-LOS-134.summary: Applications not selected advance automatically and the audit trail records them as a system decision stating the rate applied, not as a person's decision.
concept.BR-LOS-134.title: Applications not picked advance as a system decision stating the rate

concept.BR-LOS-135.summary: Sampling rates can be set globally, per partner and per product; changes need maker-checker approval, are effective-dated and are kept in a change history of six facts.
concept.BR-LOS-135.title: Sampling rates are set globally, per partner and per product, with a second approver

concept.BR-LOS-136.summary: The configuration screen shows the rate in practical terms as well as a percentage, such as how many applications it would have selected from the partner's latest batch.
concept.BR-LOS-136.title: The rate screen shows how much review work the rate creates

concept.BR-LOS-137.summary: Beyond the random rate, Credit Risk configures mandatory sampling rules for large amounts, new partners, cross-partner duplicates, referred or risky grades, requested overrides, partners with high rejection rates and new districts.
concept.BR-LOS-137.title: Some applications are always reviewed under seven mandatory rules

concept.BR-LOS-140.summary: A rejection must carry a reason code chosen from a configurable list; free text may be added but never replaces the code.
concept.BR-LOS-140.title: A rejection needs a reason code from a list; free text is extra

concept.BR-LOS-141.summary: The reviewer's identity, decision, reason and timestamp are recorded immutably against the application.
concept.BR-LOS-141.title: Each review decision is saved with who, what, why and when

concept.BR-LOS-142.summary: A reviewer can defer an application to a supervisor with a note, instead of being forced to accept or reject.
concept.BR-LOS-142.title: A reviewer may pass a case up to a supervisor with a note

concept.BR-LOS-143.summary: The review queue can be driven from the keyboard and shows the number of applications remaining.
concept.BR-LOS-143.title: The review queue is driven from the keyboard and shows how many remain

concept.BR-LOS-144.summary: A sampling decision can be reversed only by a supervisor, under maker-checker, with a reason, and the original decision stays visible in the audit trail next to the reversal.
concept.BR-LOS-144.title: Only a supervisor can reverse a review decision, and the original stays visible

concept.BR-LOS-145.summary: Sampling outcomes roll up into partner quality metrics: rejection rate overall and by reason, trend over time and comparison across partners; a breach of a configured threshold alerts the Bank and may raise that partner's rate automatically.
concept.BR-LOS-145.title: Sampling outcomes feed partner quality figures and can raise a partner's rate

concept.BR-LOS-150.summary: The app that field officers use to verify applicants must run on Android, and the bank decides the lowest Android version.
concept.BR-LOS-150.title: The field officer app runs on Android

concept.BR-LOS-151.summary: The field app may be installed and used only on a device tied to one registered officer, and a change of device needs an administrator.
concept.BR-LOS-151.title: The app is tied to one registered officer and one device

concept.BR-LOS-152.summary: Login needs credentials plus a second factor, and the app locks after a set idle time and asks the officer to sign in again.
concept.BR-LOS-152.title: Officers log in with two factors and the session locks when idle

concept.BR-LOS-153.summary: Officers can switch the app between Bangla and English at any time without losing the work they have started.
concept.BR-LOS-153.title: The app comes in Bangla and English

concept.BR-LOS-154.summary: Screens must be easy to use with one hand, with buttons big enough to press while the officer is on their feet.
concept.BR-LOS-154.title: The app can be used with one hand while standing

concept.BR-LOS-155.summary: The app should stop screenshots on any screen that shows a customer's identity data or the evidence captured from them.
concept.BR-LOS-155.title: Screenshots are blocked on screens showing identity data or evidence

concept.BR-LOS-160.summary: The app downloads each officer's assigned applications in advance and lets them finish data capture with no signal, sending it when a connection returns.
concept.BR-LOS-160.title: Officers can capture data offline and send it later

concept.BR-LOS-161.summary: Data waiting on the device must be encrypted, and once the bank confirms receipt the device deletes its copies of biometrics and identity images.
concept.BR-LOS-161.title: Offline data is encrypted and biometric copies are erased after sync

concept.BR-LOS-162.summary: If captures stay unsent past a set time they are deleted, the verification is marked abandoned, and the applicant can be assigned again.
concept.BR-LOS-162.title: Data left unsent too long is erased and the check is marked abandoned

concept.BR-LOS-163.summary: Officers can always see whether the device is online and what has been sent, and a queue screen lists each pending item.
concept.BR-LOS-163.title: Every screen shows connection and sync state, with a queue view

concept.BR-LOS-164.summary: If the app has been offline too long, its downloaded sanction details count as stale and must be refreshed before approval can go ahead.
concept.BR-LOS-164.title: Old downloaded sanction data is refreshed before approval

concept.BR-LOS-170.summary: An officer starts a verification by picking an assigned applicant or, for someone not on the list, by entering an account number and a mobile number.
concept.BR-LOS-170.title: An officer starts a verification from the list or by manual lookup

concept.BR-LOS-171.summary: At the start the app shows the officer the applicant's KYC data, the national database result and the portrait, read-only, and the officer confirms or flags a discrepancy.
concept.BR-LOS-171.title: The officer confirms the applicant's KYC details or flags a difference

concept.BR-LOS-172.summary: The app asks only for the extra fields that a given application requires, and the bank can change those fields without a software release.
concept.BR-LOS-172.title: Only the supplementary fields an application needs are shown

concept.BR-LOS-173.summary: The officer captures the applicant's signature on a full-screen canvas with stylus or finger, and it is stored as an image with a time and coordinates.
concept.BR-LOS-173.title: A wet signature is captured on screen

concept.BR-LOS-174.summary: The app takes a fingerprint with a reader on the device and shows a quality score, or with the camera if there is no hardware, in which case it has no score and is only evidence of presence.
concept.BR-LOS-174.title: A fingerprint is captured, with a quality score where hardware allows

concept.BR-LOS-175.summary: The app checks that the applicant is a live person by camera, returns pass or fail with limited retries, and compares the live image with the retained portrait.
concept.BR-LOS-175.title: A liveness check compares the live face with the retained portrait

concept.BR-LOS-176.summary: Each capture stores the device, the officer, the time and the coordinates, and a capture far from the meeting venue is flagged for Bank review, not blocked.
concept.BR-LOS-176.title: Every capture records who, when, on which device and where

concept.BR-LOS-177.summary: If an applicant exceeds the liveness attempt limit the verification halts and the applicant is referred to the Bank, and the application is not simply failed.
concept.BR-LOS-177.title: Too many failed liveness tries stop the check and refer the applicant to the Bank

concept.BR-LOS-178.summary: Once evidence has been synchronised it is fixed. A correction needs a new capture, both are kept, and the audit trail shows their order.
concept.BR-LOS-178.title: Evidence cannot be changed once sent; a correction is a new capture

concept.BR-LOS-180.summary: Sanctioned applications appear in a queue that can be grouped by partner, by district and upazila, and by scheduled meeting event.
concept.BR-LOS-180.title: Sanctioned applications wait in an assignment queue

concept.BR-LOS-181.summary: The platform keeps a record for each meeting event with its partner, venue, place, time and attendee numbers, and a whole meeting can be assigned in one action.
concept.BR-LOS-181.title: A meeting event record, with assignment for the whole meeting at once

concept.BR-LOS-182.summary: Assigning can be done in bulk, shows each officer's current workload and coverage area, and warns when an assignment would go over the officer's daily capacity.
concept.BR-LOS-182.title: Assignment can be done in bulk, with workload shown and a capacity warning

concept.BR-LOS-183.summary: An assignment can be given to someone else with a recorded reason, and one not acted on within a set time returns to the queue and is reported.
concept.BR-LOS-183.title: Assignments can be reassigned and unactioned ones go back to the queue

concept.BR-LOS-184.summary: Each field officer has a profile with nine items, including coverage areas, the bound device and effective dates.
concept.BR-LOS-184.title: A profile is kept for each field officer

concept.BR-LOS-185.summary: When an officer is suspended or deactivated, access on their bound device stops immediately and their open assignments go back to the queue.
concept.BR-LOS-185.title: Suspending an officer cuts off the app at once and returns their assignments

concept.BR-LOS-186.summary: The bank gets a report on each officer's verifications completed, average time per verification, abandonment rate, bureau pass rate and disbursement conversion.
concept.BR-LOS-186.title: Officer performance is reported on five measures

concept.BR-LOS-190.summary: The platform sends the bureau inquiry through a designated host inside the Bank's permitted network, judges the response against configured rules, and gives the device only a pass or fail.
concept.BR-LOS-190.title: The platform asks the bureau and returns only pass or fail to the device

concept.BR-LOS-191.summary: The officer's device must never receive, display, cache or log any bureau detail: not the score, exposure figures, institution names, classification or account counts.
concept.BR-LOS-191.title: The device never receives, shows, keeps or logs any bureau detail

concept.BR-LOS-192.summary: When the bureau check fails, the officer sees neutral next-step guidance that does not state or imply the reason.
concept.BR-LOS-192.title: A fail shows neutral next steps without giving or hinting at a reason

concept.BR-LOS-193.summary: The full bureau response is kept centrally and shown only to separately permissioned Bank users in a dedicated panel, and every view is logged.
concept.BR-LOS-193.title: The full bureau response is kept centrally and seen only by permitted Bank users

concept.BR-LOS-194.summary: The rules that decide pass or fail are owned by Credit Risk, versioned and approved by maker-checker, and each decision records the rule version in force at its own time.
concept.BR-LOS-194.title: Pass or fail rules are owned by Credit Risk, versioned and checked by a second person

concept.BR-LOS-195.summary: When the bureau or the designated host is unavailable the application holds and retries automatically with a clear message to the officer, and a timeout or transport error is never read as a pass.
concept.BR-LOS-195.title: If the bureau cannot be reached the application waits, and a timeout never counts as a pass

concept.BR-LOS-196.summary: Every inquiry is logged with eight items, including the raw response and the rule version, and kept for the full retention period.
concept.BR-LOS-196.title: Every bureau inquiry is logged in full and kept for the whole retention period

concept.BR-LOS-197.summary: Repeat inquiries for the same applicant within a configurable window reuse the retained response instead of asking the bureau again.
concept.BR-LOS-197.title: A repeat inquiry for the same applicant reuses the kept response

concept.BR-LOS-200.summary: Before approval the application shows the sanctioned amount, tenor, indicative instalment, rate and any fees, the officer must confirm, and any difference from the requested amount is shown plainly.
concept.BR-LOS-200.title: Before approval the officer sees the amount, tenor, instalment, rate and fees and confirms

concept.BR-LOS-201.summary: Opening the account and disbursing are two separate steps, each retryable on its own, each with a distinct platform-generated reference written into the core banking record and its own progress state.
concept.BR-LOS-201.title: Opening the loan account and paying out are two steps, each retryable with its own reference and progress

concept.BR-LOS-201a.summary: If funding cannot finish within the configured waiting period, the officer can end the visit at approved status, funding completes later, and both the borrower and the officer are told the outcome.
concept.BR-LOS-201a.title: If funding takes too long the officer can end the visit and funding finishes later

concept.BR-LOS-202.summary: Account opening must be confirmed and persisted before disbursement is attempted.
concept.BR-LOS-202.title: The account is confirmed and saved before any disbursement is tried

concept.BR-LOS-203.summary: If account opening succeeds and disbursement fails, the application holds at account opened and an exception is raised, with no silent retry loop.
concept.BR-LOS-203.title: If the account opens but payment fails, the application holds and an exception is raised

concept.BR-LOS-204.summary: Before a retry the platform re-reads the core banking system for the definitive state, never retries after an interrupted session, and records success without a second instruction if the first had executed.
concept.BR-LOS-204.title: Before any retry the platform checks what really happened and never pays twice

concept.BR-LOS-205.summary: Account validation is run again immediately before disbursement, and a dormant, closed or otherwise ineligible account halts disbursement and raises an exception.
concept.BR-LOS-205.title: The account is checked again just before payment and a bad account stops it

concept.BR-LOS-206.summary: If the automation reaches an unrecognised screen, an unexpected message or an ambiguous outcome, the platform halts, holds the application, captures the session evidence and raises an exception, and does not guess.
concept.BR-LOS-206.title: On a screen the automation does not recognise, the platform stops and does not guess

concept.BR-LOS-207.summary: Disbursement is blocked where the sanction has lapsed under BR-LOS-330 or a sanction condition remains unevidenced.
concept.BR-LOS-207.title: Payment is blocked when the sanction has lapsed or a sanction condition is not evidenced

concept.BR-LOS-208.summary: After a completed disbursement the officer sees a receipt with five items, can print and share it, and can go straight to the next applicant with the number of assignments left for the meeting event.
concept.BR-LOS-208.title: After payment the officer gets a receipt and moves on to the next applicant

concept.BR-LOS-209.summary: The borrower is notified of the disbursement through the configured channel, a failed notification is retried and reported, and it never blocks or reverses a loan action.
concept.BR-LOS-209.title: The borrower is told of the payment and a failed message never blocks or reverses the loan

concept.BR-LOS-210.summary: Bank staff can open everything a partner sees plus seven more kinds of detail, from the full bureau data to the complete audit trail.
concept.BR-LOS-210.title: Bank staff can open the full application detail, including the data a partner cannot see

concept.BR-LOS-211.summary: Bank staff can search across all applications by NID, mobile number, account number, applicant name, partner, batch reference and loan account number.
concept.BR-LOS-211.title: Bank staff can search every application by seven identifiers

concept.BR-LOS-212.summary: Bank staff can place a hold on a single application, a batch or an entire partner, which stops further progression until an investigation is done.
concept.BR-LOS-212.title: Bank staff can put a hold on one application, a batch or a whole partner

concept.BR-LOS-213.summary: An exceptions workspace lists every item that needs intervention, five kinds named by the BRD, each with an owner, an ageing indicator and a documented closure record.
concept.BR-LOS-213.title: An exceptions workspace lists every item needing action, with an owner, age and closure record

concept.BR-LOS-220.summary: Partner users can list, filter, sort and export their own applications, with six named filters.
concept.BR-LOS-220.title: Partners can list, filter, sort and export their own applications

concept.BR-LOS-221.summary: The application detail a partner sees has eight items, including a masked account number, the full status timeline, the sanctioned amount and any rejection reason.
concept.BR-LOS-221.title: Partners see a set of eight details for each of their applications

concept.BR-LOS-222.summary: Partners have no access to six kinds of data: bureau data of any kind, identity images or their scores, sampling selection or outcome detail, field officer notes, internal reference data, or another partner's data.
concept.BR-LOS-222.title: Partners never see bureau data, identity images, scores, sampling, officer notes or another partner's data

concept.BR-LOS-223.summary: Partners have a disbursed-accounts view with five items, taken from servicing.
concept.BR-LOS-223.title: Partners get a view of their disbursed accounts taken from servicing

concept.BR-LOS-224.summary: Partners can generate and schedule reports on batch summary, approval funnel, rejection reasons by category and disbursement register, exportable to XLSX and CSV.
concept.BR-LOS-224.title: Partners can create and schedule four reports and export them as XLSX and CSV

concept.BR-LOS-225.summary: The portal shows a dashboard with pipeline volumes and values by status, conversion and drop-off by stage, and items awaiting partner action. This one is a Should.
concept.BR-LOS-225.title: The partner portal shows a dashboard of pipeline, conversion and items awaiting the partner

concept.BR-LOS-230.summary: Platform administrators manage users, roles and function-level permissions for Bank and partner organisations, with onboarding by invitation and a forced password reset on first use.
concept.BR-LOS-230.title: Administrators manage users, roles and permissions for the Bank and partners

concept.BR-LOS-231.summary: Product configuration is to include product code and name, minimum and maximum ticket, permitted tenors, rate and fee structure, eligibility rules and required application fields.
concept.BR-LOS-231.title: Product configuration sets the code, ticket sizes, tenors, rates, fees, eligibility and fields

concept.BR-LOS-232.summary: All configuration is versioned and effective-dated, with a change history showing before value, after value, maker, checker, timestamp and justification.
concept.BR-LOS-232.title: All configuration is versioned and dated, with a change history

concept.BR-LOS-233.summary: The platform records, against every decision, the configuration version in force at that moment, so a past decision can be explained by the rules then applying.
concept.BR-LOS-233.title: Every decision records the configuration version in force so it can be explained later

concept.BR-LOS-234.summary: Reference data such as districts, upazilas, loan purposes, rejection reason codes and supplementary field definitions can be maintained without a software release.
concept.BR-LOS-234.title: Reference data can be changed without a software release

concept.BR-LOS-235.summary: Configuration can be exported and imported between environments, so a change can be promoted from test to production in a controlled way. This one is a Should.
concept.BR-LOS-235.title: Configuration can be exported and imported between environments

concept.BR-LOS-240.summary: The platform presents one dashboard of the origination pipeline: volume and value by status, funnel conversion and drop-off, ageing, a partner league table and field officer utilisation.
concept.BR-LOS-240.title: An operational dashboard shows the application pipeline

concept.BR-LOS-241.summary: The platform has a standard set of six origination reports, from a batch summary to a disbursement register.
concept.BR-LOS-241.title: A standard set of origination reports

concept.BR-LOS-242.summary: Origination reports can be exported to XLSX and CSV, run on a schedule, and sent to chosen recipients by email.
concept.BR-LOS-242.title: Origination reports can be exported, scheduled and emailed

concept.BR-LOS-250.summary: The platform produces the data extracts the bank needs for Bangladesh Bank agricultural and rural credit reporting; the bank is to supply the formats.
concept.BR-LOS-250.title: Data extracts for Bangladesh Bank agricultural and rural credit reporting

concept.BR-LOS-300.summary: The platform scores every submitted application against the scorecard for its product and does not move an unscored application to sampling or to sanction.
concept.BR-LOS-300.title: Every submitted application is scored before it moves on

concept.BR-LOS-301.summary: The scorecard can draw on application data, derived ratios, geography, account behaviour, the partner's track record, credit bureau data and duplicate, negative-list and mandatory-sampling flags.
concept.BR-LOS-301.title: The scorecard can use seven kinds of input

concept.BR-LOS-302.summary: Scorecards are configuration owned by Credit Risk; attributes, bands, weights, exclusions and cut-offs can be changed without a release, and every change is versioned, effective-dated and approved by a second person with a stated reason.
concept.BR-LOS-302.title: Credit Risk owns the scorecard and changes it without a software release

concept.BR-LOS-303.summary: Scoring produces a numeric score, a risk grade and a recommended decision of auto-approve, refer or decline, set by cut-offs that can differ by product and partner.
concept.BR-LOS-303.title: Scoring gives a score, a risk grade and a recommended decision

concept.BR-LOS-304.summary: Every score is stored with the scorecard version, every attribute value used, each attribute's contribution, the cut-offs in force and the resulting grade and recommendation, and the record cannot be altered.
concept.BR-LOS-304.title: Each score is recorded and cannot be changed afterwards

concept.BR-LOS-305.summary: Every refer and decline records the main adverse factors as reason codes from a configurable list, so the Bank can explain the decision inside and, where required, to the applicant.
concept.BR-LOS-305.title: Refer and decline outcomes carry reason codes

concept.BR-LOS-306.summary: The risk grade can drive a cap on amount, a cap on tenor, a pricing tier, extra verification or a security requirement, and a capped amount keeps both the requested and capped figures.
concept.BR-LOS-306.title: The risk grade can set limits and extra steps on the loan offered

concept.BR-LOS-307.summary: Referred applications are always sampled, grade bands carry their own sampling rate, and auto-approve bands may be sampled at a reduced rate that never falls to zero.
concept.BR-LOS-307.title: The score feeds sampling, with a floor that is never zero

concept.BR-LOS-308.summary: An application declined by score takes a distinct final status with reason codes, is not given to a field officer, and is reported to the partner as declined without the score, grade or scorecard logic.
concept.BR-LOS-308.title: A score-declined application gets its own final status and is not shown the score

concept.BR-LOS-309.summary: A user with delegated authority can override a score-driven decision under maker-checker with a mandatory reason; overrides are recorded, reported separately and watched for volume and later performance.
concept.BR-LOS-309.title: An authorised person can override a score decision, with a second approver and a reason

concept.BR-LOS-310.summary: An absent or unavailable input never silently defaults to a favourable value; the configured treatment is applied and recorded, and an absent mandatory input leads to a referral, not an auto-approval.
concept.BR-LOS-310.title: Absent data is never treated as good news

concept.BR-LOS-311.summary: The platform can run a second scorecard in shadow, recording its outcome without acting on it, so a new scorecard can be tested on live applications before adoption.
concept.BR-LOS-311.title: A second scorecard can run quietly alongside the live one

concept.BR-LOS-312.summary: The platform reports score and grade distribution, approval and decline rates by grade, override volume and reason, spread by partner and geography and, once servicing data is in use, delinquency and loss by grade band.
concept.BR-LOS-312.title: Scorecard performance is reported so the scorecard can be recalibrated

concept.BR-LOS-313.summary: The Bank can reproduce, for any past application, the score, attribute values, grade, cut-offs and scorecard version in force at decision time, whatever changed later.
concept.BR-LOS-313.title: Any past decision can be reproduced as it was at the time

concept.BR-LOS-314.summary: The score, grade, attribute contributions and scorecard logic are never sent to, shown on, cached or logged by the field officer's device; the officer sees only the terms to confirm.
concept.BR-LOS-314.title: The field officer's device never holds the score or its logic

concept.BR-LOS-320.summary: The platform sets the proposed amount, tenor, rate and fees from the product setting, the risk grade's treatment, the partner's remaining headroom and the borrower's total exposure.
concept.BR-LOS-320.title: The proposed sanction is set from product, grade, headroom and borrower exposure

concept.BR-LOS-321.summary: The platform sanctions automatically only where the application is within every auto-sanction threshold; thresholds are set by amount band, risk grade, tenor, product and partner, versioned, effective-dated and approved by a second person.
concept.BR-LOS-321.title: Automatic sanction only inside every configured threshold

concept.BR-LOS-322.summary: An application outside an auto-sanction threshold goes to a credit approval queue and cannot move to assignment until a credit approver has decided it.
concept.BR-LOS-322.title: Outside a threshold, the case waits in a credit approval queue

concept.BR-LOS-323.summary: The credit approver sees on one screen the KYC, account result, grade and reasons, bureau data, flags, sampling outcome, partner context, borrower exposure and proposed terms.
concept.BR-LOS-323.title: The credit approver sees the whole case on one screen

concept.BR-LOS-324.summary: The credit approver can sanction as proposed, sanction at revised terms, sanction subject to conditions, defer to a higher authority with a note, or decline; a decline and a revision each need a reason code from a list.
concept.BR-LOS-324.title: The approver has five ways to decide, and declines and revisions need reason codes

concept.BR-LOS-325.summary: An approver cannot sanction above their limit; the application escalates to the next authority level and the escalation is recorded.
concept.BR-LOS-325.title: Delegated authority is enforced at the moment of decision

concept.BR-LOS-326.summary: An approver cannot sanction an application they reviewed at sampling or one from an organisation their account is linked to; where dual sanction is required, the second approver is a different user.
concept.BR-LOS-326.title: Approvers cannot approve their own sampled cases or their own organisation's, and dual sanction needs two people

concept.BR-LOS-327.summary: Conditions are recorded as structured items, shown to the field officer at verification and evidenced before the application can be approved; an unmet condition halts it and refers it back to the approver.
concept.BR-LOS-327.title: Conditions on a sanction are recorded, checked in the field and must be evidenced

concept.BR-LOS-328.summary: Each sanction records whether the system or a user decided, the rule or authority relied on, scorecard and configuration versions, proposed and final terms, reason codes and time; a system sanction is never recorded against a user.
concept.BR-LOS-328.title: Every sanction is recorded as a system or user decision with the rules relied on

concept.BR-LOS-329.summary: Applications awaiting credit approval show how long they have waited, escalate automatically after a configured period and are reported with their ageing so that a queue does not delay a scheduled meeting event.
concept.BR-LOS-329.title: Cases awaiting approval age visibly and escalate on their own

concept.BR-LOS-330.summary: A sanction lapses after a configured validity period; a lapsed sanction blocks assignment and disbursement and needs a new sanction, with score and account check refreshed where they have expired.
concept.BR-LOS-330.title: A sanction lapses after a set validity period

concept.BR-LOS-331.summary: Before sanction the platform adds up the borrower's exposure across every application and loan on the platform, and across the Bank where it can be retrieved, and applies the single-borrower limit.
concept.BR-LOS-331.title: The borrower's total exposure is added up before sanction and held to a limit

concept.BR-LOS-332.summary: No sanction is issued where identity verification has failed, a mandatory validation is outstanding, or the partner's exposure ceiling would be breached.
concept.BR-LOS-332.title: No sanction if identity failed, a validation is outstanding or the ceiling would break

concept.BR-LOS-333.summary: The platform reports sanction activity: auto against approver-sanctioned volume, declines and reasons, revisions and average reduction, approver throughput and queue ageing, and escalations by authority level.
concept.BR-LOS-333.title: Sanction activity is reported

decision.freeze.summary: A freeze suspends a loan's processing for an authorised period. The BRD wants the approval, the period and the suspended processing recorded. Frappe Lending has a tick box with a log that has no approver and, in the test, no reason, and unfreezing charged the frozen days.
decision.freeze.title: Decision: freezing a loan

decision.override.summary: An override lets an authorised person change a loan's grade against the days-past-due bands, with a reason and an approver. Frappe Lending's only override is the Manual NPA tick, with no reason, approver or history.
decision.override.title: Decision: overriding a loan's classification by hand

decision.restructure.summary: A restructure changes a loan's terms for a borrower who struggles to pay. The BRD wants two people, limits by branch and period, and reporting to Bangladesh Bank. Frappe Lending has none of the three controls.
decision.restructure.title: Decision: restructuring or rescheduling a loan

decision.settlement.summary: A settlement closes a loan for an agreed figure, which may include waivers. The BRD wants the make-up shown before approval and two people to approve. Frappe Lending shows the make-up on the repayment form and has no approval step.
decision.settlement.title: Decision: settling a loan for less than the full amount

decision.waiver.summary: A waiver forgives part of what a borrower owes. The BRD wants two people and an amount limit by role. Frappe Lending lets one Loan Manager do it alone.
decision.waiver.title: Decision: waiving an amount owed

decision.write-off.summary: A write-off removes an unrecoverable balance from the books while keeping the loan's history. The BRD wants a threshold, two people and limits by amount. Frappe Lending can write off automatically with no approver.
decision.write-off.title: Decision: writing off a loan balance

devitem.D1.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that accepts one complete handoff package for a funded loan, rejects incomplete ones into an exception queue and books the loan and its payout together.
devitem.D1.title: D1 Funded-loan handoff intake

devitem.D10.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that adds reports to check that interest, payments and partner positions agree across the records, and raises an exception for anything unmatched.
devitem.D10.title: D10 Reconciliation reports

devitem.D11.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending for changing the interest rate of many floating-rate loans at once: select, practice run, second-person approval, then one safe job per loan and a notice to the borrower.
devitem.D11.title: D11 Loan Repricing Run

devitem.D12.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that confirms payments with the CBS, blocks duplicate references and holds unmatched money in an owned queue.
devitem.D12.title: D12 Payment confirmation and receipts

devitem.D13.summary: A planned add-on, sized L, that sends accounting entries to the CBS through a software robot and brings back the CBS journal number.
devitem.D13.title: D13 CBS and RPA posting bridge

devitem.D14.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that works out, stores and optionally posts the money set aside against expected loan losses, by class and by security cover.
devitem.D14.title: D14 Provisioning engine

devitem.D15.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that records each change of a loan's grade and lets a named person override the grade with a reason and an approver. Verification made it larger.
devitem.D15.title: D15 Classification history and override

devitem.D16.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that records how Bangladesh Bank classifies each restructure or reschedule and reports it, without re-ageing the loan. Verification made it larger.
devitem.D16.title: D16 Bangladesh Bank treatment

devitem.D17.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending for chasing late payers: contact history, promises to pay, follow-ups and escalation to recovery. Verification showed the base module is develop only, so it is a much bigger item.
devitem.D17.title: D17 Collections escalation

devitem.D18.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that records a settlement offer, shows its make-up before any money moves, and creates the settlement entries only after approval. Verification made it larger.
devitem.D18.title: D18 Settlement proposal

devitem.D19.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that reports a co-lending partner's share of what was disbursed, collected and is outstanding, with the partner's days past due and the guarantee used. This is our item D19, not the BRD's dependency D19.
devitem.D19.title: D19 Co-lending reports

devitem.D2.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that gives each loan one BRD servicing status and keeps a log of every change, without touching Frappe's own status field.
devitem.D2.title: D2 Servicing status and log

devitem.D20.summary: Three small planned add-ons to Frappe Lending: a tracked remedy for a collateral shortfall, a per-payment choice between a lower EMI and a shorter tenor, and a closure letter with a notification. Verification made two of them larger.
devitem.D20.title: D20 Small items

devitem.D3.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that checks the totals of an imported loan book against the old system and holds the loans out of daily processing until someone signs off. Verification made it larger.
devitem.D3.title: D3 Migration control gate

devitem.D4.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that records whether a loan's rate is fixed or floating, which benchmark it follows, the spread and when it reprices.
devitem.D4.title: D4 Floating-rate setup

devitem.D5.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that makes product and risk rules versioned, effective-dated and approved by a second person, and stamps the version used on each loan record.
devitem.D5.title: D5 Versioned, approved configuration

devitem.D6.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that links each repayment plan to the one that replaced it, records what triggered the change, and shows a what-if view without saving anything.
devitem.D6.title: D6 Schedule versions, triggers and what-if

devitem.D7.summary: A planned extension of Frappe Lending's existing outstanding report so that staff can see what a borrower owed on a chosen date, by component. Verification made it smaller than first planned.
devitem.D7.title: D7 Dues as on a date

devitem.D8.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that puts a second-person approval, a reason and before-and-after amounts on the manual corrections the BRD controls. Verification made it larger.
devitem.D8.title: D8 Approval and audit pack

devitem.D9.summary: A planned add-on to Frappe Lending that gives each batch job a status and a per-loan result, a queue for things that go wrong, alerts on job failure and a two-step bulk payment upload. Verification made it larger.
devitem.D9.title: D9 Batch run and exception framework

glossary.advance-payment.summary: Paying one or more future instalments before they fall due. It is not the same as a prepayment, which cuts the principal.
glossary.advance-payment.title: Advance payment

glossary.allocation-order.summary: The set order in which a payment clears what a borrower owes, for example penalty, then interest, then principal.
glossary.allocation-order.title: Allocation order (offset sequence)

glossary.application.summary: One prospective loan. In a partner's file, one row is one application.
glossary.application.title: Application

glossary.asset-classification.summary: The risk category a loan is placed in, worked out from days past due and, where the bank wishes, a person's judgement.
glossary.asset-classification.title: Asset classification (loan grade)

glossary.batch.summary: In the BRD's definitions, one file uploaded by a partner with many applications. In Section 7 the word is also used for a job that runs over many loans at once.
glossary.batch.title: Batch

glossary.bb.summary: Bangladesh's central bank and regulator. It sets the classification, provisioning and reporting rules the bank follows.
glossary.bb.title: BB (Bangladesh Bank)

glossary.bpi.summary: Interest for the odd days between payout and the first regular due date, which do not fit the normal instalment cycle.
glossary.bpi.title: BPI (broken-period interest)

glossary.cbs.summary: The bank's main system. It holds the real customer accounts and money, and the loan system must agree with it.
glossary.cbs.title: CBS (Core Banking System)

glossary.cib.summary: Bangladesh Bank's credit bureau, the source of a borrower's credit history.
glossary.cib.title: CIB (Credit Information Bureau)

glossary.cif.summary: The customer master record inside the bank's core banking system.
glossary.cif.title: CIF (Customer Information File)

glossary.cr-dr.summary: The two sides of an accounting entry. Each posting debits one account and credits another.
glossary.cr-dr.title: Cr and Dr (credit and debit)

glossary.demand.summary: An amount the bank has formally raised as due for payment, such as an instalment, principal, interest, a penalty or a charge.
glossary.demand.title: Demand

glossary.dpd.summary: How many days an amount has been overdue. It drives the loan's grade and whether it becomes a non-performing loan.
glossary.dpd.title: DPD (days past due)

glossary.ecdb.summary: The national identity database against which an applicant's identity is checked.
glossary.ecdb.title: ECDB (Election Commission Database)

glossary.effective-date.summary: The date from which a change of terms or rate applies. It is a different date from the value date, and the BRD asks for them to be kept apart.
glossary.effective-date.title: Effective date

glossary.ekyc.summary: Identity checking on a phone or tablet: a check against the national database, a liveness test and a face match.
glossary.ekyc.title: eKYC (electronic know your customer)

glossary.emi.summary: The same amount paid every month, made of part principal and part interest.
glossary.emi.title: EMI (equated monthly instalment)

glossary.fd-fdr.summary: A fixed deposit is a term deposit. Its receipt, the FDR, can be pledged as collateral or held as a partner's guarantee money.
glossary.fd-fdr.title: FD and FDR (fixed deposit, fixed deposit receipt)

glossary.field-officer.summary: A bank staff member who meets applicants in person at a partner's gathering to verify them.
glossary.field-officer.title: Field Officer

glossary.fldg.summary: A promise by a co-lending partner to cover the first part of any losses, up to an agreed share.
glossary.fldg.title: FLDG (first-loss default guarantee)

glossary.gl.summary: The bank's main accounting book, where the money effects of loan activity are recorded as debits and credits.
glossary.gl.title: GL (general ledger)

glossary.idempotency.summary: A rule that doing the same thing twice has the effect of doing it once, so a repeated instruction cannot create a duplicate payment or posting.
glossary.idempotency.title: Idempotency

glossary.income-suspense.summary: A ledger treatment that stops counting certain unpaid interest as normal earnings. It waits in a holding account until the money is actually recovered.
glossary.income-suspense.title: Income suspense

glossary.irac.summary: An Indian rule set for when to count interest as income and how to grade loans. Frappe Lending uses this name for its provisioning table.
glossary.irac.title: IRAC (income recognition and asset classification)

glossary.lms.summary: The system that looks after a loan after the money has been paid out: schedule, interest, repayments, overdue, closure.
glossary.lms.title: LMS (loan management system)

glossary.loc.summary: A revolving facility with an approved limit that the borrower can draw on, repay and draw on again.
glossary.loc.title: LOC (line of credit)

glossary.los.summary: The system that handles a loan before payout: application, scoring, checks, approval and disbursement.
glossary.los.title: LOS (loan origination system)

glossary.ltv.summary: The loan amount compared with the value of the collateral behind it. A high figure means thin cover.
glossary.ltv.title: LTV (loan to value)

glossary.maker-checker.summary: A control where one person prepares an action and a second, different person approves it before it takes effect.
glossary.maker-checker.title: Maker-checker (dual control)

glossary.meeting-event.summary: A gathering arranged by a partner where eligible applicants and Bank field officers are both present.
glossary.meeting-event.title: Meeting event

glossary.mfs.summary: Mobile money such as bKash or Nagad, one of the ways a borrower might repay.
glossary.mfs.title: MFS (mobile financial services)

glossary.mis.summary: Management information system: management reports. The BRD's Section 8 is headed with it.
glossary.mis.title: MIS (management information system)

glossary.moratorium.summary: An approved period during which some payments are put off. How interest is treated in that period follows the product's terms.
glossary.moratorium.title: Moratorium (payment holiday)

glossary.nid.summary: The national identity document, whose number identifies a person for duplicate checks and identity verification.
glossary.nid.title: NID (National Identity Document)

glossary.npa.summary: A loan that has become a bad loan: overdue beyond the bank's limit, so its unpaid interest stops counting as income.
glossary.npa.title: NPA (non-performing asset)

glossary.partner.summary: A third party that finds borrowers for the bank, such as an agricultural fintech or a device financier.
glossary.partner.title: Partner

glossary.penal-interest.summary: Extra interest charged on overdue amounts, kept apart from the normal interest, under the bank's policy.
glossary.penal-interest.title: Penal interest

glossary.pos.summary: The principal still owed on a loan. One co-lending schedule type is built on it.
glossary.pos.title: POS (principal outstanding)

glossary.posting-date.summary: The day an entry was recorded in the loan system. It can be later than the day the money moved.
glossary.posting-date.title: Posting date

glossary.prepayment.summary: Paying principal early, outside the normal schedule, so the loan shrinks. It differs from an advance payment, which pays future instalments early.
glossary.prepayment.title: Prepayment

glossary.provisioning.summary: Money the bank sets aside against expected loan losses, based on a loan's class and how well it is secured.
glossary.provisioning.title: Provisioning

glossary.ptp.summary: A borrower's promise to pay a set amount by a set date. If the date passes without payment, it is a broken promise.
glossary.ptp.title: PTP (promise to pay)

glossary.repricing.summary: A change, from a chosen date onwards, to the interest rate of an eligible floating-rate loan.
glossary.repricing.title: Repricing

glossary.rescheduling.summary: Changing the payment dates or the tenor of a loan to help a borrower who struggles to repay, or for another approved need.
glossary.rescheduling.title: Rescheduling

glossary.restructuring.summary: A wider change to the financial terms of a loan, which may include the rate, tenor, instalments, capitalisation or settlement.
glossary.restructuring.title: Restructuring

glossary.rpa.summary: Software that works another system through its screens, as a person would, when that system has no programming interface.
glossary.rpa.title: RPA (robotic process automation)

glossary.sampling.summary: Manual review of a randomly selected part of the submitted applications.
glossary.sampling.title: Sampling

glossary.sanctioned-amount.summary: The amount the bank agrees to lend, which can be lower than the amount the applicant asked for.
glossary.sanctioned-amount.title: Sanctioned amount

glossary.schedule-version.summary: One saved generation of a loan's repayment plan. When later terms produce a new plan, the old version is kept, not overwritten.
glossary.schedule-version.title: Schedule version

glossary.score-cut-off.summary: The score at which the recommended decision changes between auto-approve, refer and decline.
glossary.score-cut-off.title: Score cut-off

glossary.scorecard.summary: The set of questions, bands, weights and cut-offs that turns an application into a score and a risk grade.
glossary.scorecard.title: Scorecard

glossary.sma.summary: An early-warning grade for a loan that is late but not yet non-performing.
glossary.sma.title: SMA (special mention account)

glossary.ss.summary: The first non-performing class. In the guide's example bands it starts at 90 days past due.
glossary.ss.title: SS (sub-standard)

glossary.std.summary: A healthy loan, paid on time or only slightly late.
glossary.std.title: STD (standard)

glossary.value-date.summary: The day the money really arrived, which is the date lateness and interest follow.
glossary.value-date.title: Value date

glossary.waiver.summary: The bank's approved cancellation of an amount a borrower owes. It is not a cash payment.
glossary.waiver.title: Waiver

glossary.write-off.summary: The accounting removal of a balance the bank does not expect to recover. The borrower may still owe it, depending on policy and law.
glossary.write-off.title: Write-off

howto.company.view_loan_settings.summary: Day-count convention, loan accounting switches, grade bands and provision rates are Company settings shared by every product; they are plain tables with no version, effective date or approval.
howto.company.view_loan_settings.title: How to read the company-level loan settings (view only)

howto.customer.create.summary: Create the Customer record that a loan is booked against: name and type, then Save.
howto.customer.create.title: How to create a borrower (Customer)

howto.data_import.migrate_loan.summary: A migrated loan is a normal Loan with Is Imported, Migration Date and an opening balance row, loaded through Data Import. It needs Administrator today.
howto.data_import.migrate_loan.title: How to bring an old loan over with Data Import

howto.days_past_due_log.view.summary: The Days Past Due Log keeps one row per loan per date; the loan itself shows the current days past due and grade.
howto.days_past_due_log.view.title: How to read a loan's days past due, in the log and on the loan

howto.error_log.view_and_assign.summary: A failed batch shows as Error Log rows naming the loan; a row can be assigned to a person as a ToDo, but there is no work queue, closing note or escalation.
howto.error_log.view_and_assign.title: How to find a failed batch in the Error Log and assign it

howto.general_ledger.view_partner_positi.summary: The General Ledger on the partner's accounts is the only partner position there is; the Loan Partner form has no linked loans, ledger or balance, and no settlement or reconciliation document exists.
howto.general_ledger.view_partner_positi.title: How to see a co-lending partner's position

howto.item.create_fee.summary: Loan charge types are ordinary ERPNext Items, so a processing fee starts as a non-stock service Item.
howto.item.create_fee.title: How to create a fee item for a loan charge

howto.loan.auto_close_credit_line.summary: A scheduled job closes an Active line-of-credit loan once its limit end date has passed and nothing is drawn; it has no screen, no loan filter, no approval and no notification.
howto.loan.auto_close_credit_line.title: How a line-of-credit loan is closed automatically

howto.loan.change_credit_limit.summary: The maximum limit can be raised or cut on the Loan and every change leaves a Loan Limit Change Log row, but there is no reason or approver and a large cut needs no approval.
howto.loan.change_credit_limit.title: How to change a credit line's limit and read the log

howto.loan.choose_co_lender.summary: Choosing a Loan Partner on the loan books the partner's share on disbursement, on its own schedule and on each demand and first repayment; a Loan Closure posts nothing to the partner.
howto.loan.choose_co_lender.title: How to book a co-lent loan and see the partner's share

howto.loan.create.summary: Create a Loan for a borrower with the product, amount and dates, tick Auto create disbursement, and Save as a draft.
howto.loan.create.title: How to book a loan with auto-disbursement

howto.loan.filter_list.summary: The Loan list can be filtered and the filter saved, which is the workaround for an overdue work list and for a repricing selection; the list has no arrears column.
howto.loan.filter_list.title: How to build a working list of loans with a filter

howto.loan.follow_up.summary: The collections module of the BRD does not exist in 16.5.1; the workaround is a saved overdue list, an assignment with a follow-up date, and comments on the loan.
howto.loan.follow_up.title: How to chase an overdue loan without a collections screen

howto.loan.freeze.summary: Ticking Freeze Account on the Totals tab freezes a loan with no reason, approver or confirmation, and the Loan Freeze Log records the date but no reason.
howto.loan.freeze.title: How to freeze a loan and read the Freeze Log

howto.loan.submit.summary: Submitting the draft loan disburses it: Frappe Lending creates the disbursement and the repayment schedule in the same action.
howto.loan.submit.title: How to submit a loan

howto.loan.view.summary: Open a loan to see which product rules it picked up, how much was drawn, and everything linked to it on the Connections tab.
howto.loan.view.title: How to check a loan: rules, amounts and connections

howto.loan.view_grade.summary: The loan shows its days past due and grade from the company's bands; the only manual override is the NPA tick, and no history of grade changes is kept.
howto.loan.view_grade.title: How to read a loan's grade (SMA) and what can override it

howto.loan_accrual_repost.create.summary: A Loan Accrual Repost only repairs missing ledger entries of accruals that are still submitted; a cancelled day is never booked again, so it cannot redo interest for a period.
howto.loan_accrual_repost.create.title: How to repost interest for a period

howto.loan_balance_adjustment.create.summary: A credit or debit adjustment moves the pending principal against an account the user picks, with no approval step; its reason and reference are optional.
howto.loan_balance_adjustment.create.title: How to correct a loan balance with a Loan Balance Adjustment

howto.loan_demand.cancel.summary: An unpaid Loan Demand is cancelled in one click with no reason or approver; a partly paid one is blocked by its link to the repayment, with a Cancel All shortcut.
howto.loan_demand.cancel.title: How to cancel a wrong bill
